description:
**Job Description**
Sr. Analyst/Associate: Corporate Planning & Management – Contingent Workforce Management
  
  
Divisional Overview
  
  
The Corporate Planning & Management (CPM) Division unifies Finance & Planning, Spend Management, Operational Risk and Resilience, and CPM Engineering teams to deliver business planning and analytics, expense management, third party risk management, and governance strategies across the firm. CPM has 5 operating pillars: Finance & Planning supports the execution of the firm’s strategic objectives through the management of the planning process, firmwide reporting and analytics and insights into the firm’s business plans and budgets. They develop consistent framework for revenue division projections creating transparency, accountability and efficiency around projections. This pillar also includes the CF&O, EO and Engineering divisional CFOs, who are strategic finance advisors helping the firm and the non-revenue divisions achieve commercial financial opportunities. Product Finance is responsible for the overall governance and proactive management of the firm’s non-compensation expenses. Spend Management encompasses the functions responsible for managing all aspects of the firm's spend with third parties - advising commercial agreements and driving operating efficiency. Departments include Strategic Sourcing, Procure to Pay, Integrated Travel and Expense, Infrastructure and Transformation and Sustainable Operations. Operational Risk & Resilience (ORR) drives firmwide Operational Risk programs along with second line teams and implements required changes within CPM. This pillar also includes the Contingent Workforce Management team, CWM Team ensures effective execution of contingent workforce controls by providing oversight and guidance, managing CW risks, incidents, reporting and compliance activities, maintaining accurate worker records and management tools, supporting policy interpretation and exception management, and overseeing end-to-end operational processes including vendor coordination, onboarding/offboarding, data integrity, and escalation of CW-related risks and policy violations. The CPM Engineering team provides engineering solutions that enable the firm to manage third-party spend, data and automation, plan budgets, forecast financial scenarios, allocate expenses and support corporate decision making in-line with the firm’s strategic objectives.
  
  
Role Overview
  
  
Professionals in CPM have an analytical mindset, exhibit intellectual curiosity and are from diverse academic backgrounds. The Associate level role is based in Bangalore and sits within Unified Contingent workforce team which is responsible for the governance and operations of the contingent workforce of the firm. CWM Team is responsible for the implementation, maintenance, oversight, and periodic review of the Policy and Standard. Through its governance and operations functions, CWM Team ensures effective execution of contingent workforce controls by providing oversight and guidance, managing CW risks, incidents, reporting and compliance activities, maintaining accurate worker records and management tools, supporting policy interpretation and exception management, and overseeing end-to-end operational processes including vendor coordination, onboarding/offboarding, data integrity, and escalation of CW-related risks and policy violations.
  
  
The role requires collaboration with senior leadership across the firm on a regular basis, an ability to work independently, have a strategic mindset and communication with impact that helps driving firm’s 3.0 strategies and projects. It also entails in-depth analysis and reporting for senior management, requiring diligence, risk and a commercial mindset. The candidate is required to work closely with global counterparts. Should have excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  
  
**Job Responsibilities Will Include, But Are Not Limited To**

* Become a Subject Matter Expert of the Contingent Workforce Policies and Standards, including process governance and controls, risk management
* Act as a key advisor to internal stakeholders and help address queries related to the risk and governance of CWs
* Build strong business relationships with teammates and stakeholders firmwide to understand impact of the Program requirements based on the business and divisional initiatives
* Partner with the team to support deliver on and further evolve the India/regional process nuances
* Participate and support CWM team for timely responses to risk teams and 2nd Line reviews (e.g., Compliance, Internal Audit, Operational Risk)
* Identify and lead unified CW Program enhancements driven by evolving process and user experience demand
* Drive projects for continuous process and user experience improvement and bring innovation into the team
* Lead initiatives / strategies from inception to completion
* Communicate progress and decision points for projects to relevant functions and maintain key documentation of approvals where required
* Coordinate input into firmwide transformation initiatives impacting (CW) Programs (e.g., vendor onboarding transformation, Contingent worker on-boarding transformation, Gating council, ODC etc.)
* Maintain CW program(s) documentation (e.g., policies, standards, procedures, reference guides, training content) to ensure consistency with program initiatives, and broader CWM transformation priorities
* Coordinate content for internal senior forums and divisional leadership engagement meetings (e.g., Committees, Governance Groups, etc.)
* Oversight of business-as-usual Program components (i.e, reviewing queries, CW dashboard and exception requests from other divisions and business units)
* Engage, initiate, contribute and deliver on regional expectations

**Qualifications**

* Relevant Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification with an excellent academic record
* 3-5 years of relevant experience in the field of risk, Contingent workforce, and/or business management
* Analytical capabilities and leadership facing experience
* Excellent communication and interpersonal (written and verbal) skills, strong attention to detail
* Ability to lead across team members and drive assignments to completion
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple competing deadlines
* Solid work ethic and high level of motivation
* Proficient in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint

title: Senior Specialist-Corporate Paralegal
description:
**Fresenius Medical Care**
is the premier health care company focused on delivering the highest quality of care to people with renal and other chronic conditions. Through our industry-leading global network of more than 3,400 dialysis clinics and acute care canters, outpatient cardiac and vascular labs, Fresenius Medical Care provides coordinated health care services at pivotal care points for hundreds of thousands of chronically ill patients. As the world’s only vertically integrated renal company, we also offer specialty pharmacy and laboratory services, as well as manufacturing and distributing the most comprehensive line of dialysis equipment, disposable products and renal pharmaceuticals.
  
  
Fresenius Medical Care is a people business. Our success depends on having the best and brightest employees and helping them attain their personal and professional goals while delivering excellence in patient care and business results. Our employees embody our culture which is based on core values supporting our promise to improve the quality of life of every patient every day. These core values are:
**We Care. We Connect. We Commit.**
**Role Summary**
The Corporate Paralegal provides paralegal-level support for Fresenius Medical Care's ("FME") corporate housekeeping, entity governance and transaction-related administration across FME group affiliates worldwide, working under the guidance of supervising attorneys. The role executes defined corporate administration tasks and routine stakeholder.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
***Corporate Housekeeping & Entity Portfolio Support***

* Support corporate housekeeping matters and coordinate routine legal guidance/advice requests pertaining to FME group affiliates worldwide, under attorney and senior paralegal direction
* Draft, prepare and coordinate standard corporate law documents (by-laws, resolutions, etc.) for defined, routine matters, compiling relevant corporate information
* Maintain and update the FME group entity database, supporting data accuracy and completeness under senior paralegal oversight
* Prepare corporate registration documents and support registrations with relevant institutions (e.g. companies house, local courts) for routine filings
* Support other registration and publication requirements, coordinating measures, steps and documentation as directed

***Governance Support***

* Support governance activities across FME group entities (e.g. board/shareholder actions) by coordinating documentation and process execution under attorney and senior paralegal direction
* Track adherence to internal governance requirements for assigned matters, escalating approval and interpretation questions to the supervising attorneys

***Transaction Support***

* Support M&A, financing and other corporate transactions by preparing and coordinating routine transaction-related documentation (powers of attorney, resolutions, confirmations, representations, etc.), under attorney and senior paralegal direction
* Support closing mechanics and documentation checklists for assigned transactions

***External Stakeholder Coordination***

* Prepare and coordinate routine interactions with notaries public, courts, embassies, consulates and other public institutions relevant to FME group entities, within a clearly defined, attorney-authorized scope
* Support internal and external stakeholder communications relevant to corporate housekeeping and transaction administration

**Level-Specific Scope**

* Executes defined corporate housekeeping, governance-support and transaction-administration tasks independently with limited supervision; makes decisions on moderately complex issues, typically requiring interpretation of established procedure
* Escalates complex, ambiguous or precedent-setting matters to the supervising attorneys rather than resolving them independently
* Contributions begin to influence team-level process improvements but do not set governance policy or transaction strategy
* Represents FME in coordination with external institutions (notaries, courts, registries) within a narrowly defined, attorney-authorized scope, typically for routine or lower-risk matters
* Modifies existing administrative processes to fit specific matters; does not redesign governance or transaction-support processes

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree required; paralegal certification or equivalent legal-support qualification preferred; no law degree or bar admission required
* Bachelor's degree with approximately 4–8 years of relevant experience (or Master's degree with 3+ years), including experience in corporate paralegal or entity administration work, ideally supporting multi-jurisdictional group structures in a multinational or shared-services/GBS environment
* Familiarity with corporate entity databases and registration processes across multiple jurisdictions
* Exposure to M&A or financing transaction documentation (powers of attorney, resolutions, closing checklists) is a plus
* Strong organizational and drafting skills; high attention to detail
* Excellent written and spoken English required; additional languages an advantage given the global entity portfolio
* Discretion and ability to handle confidential corporate and transactional information

**Our offer:**

* Growth Opportunity: Be part of the dynamic growth and transformation of Fresenius Medical Care India Global Hub.
* Career Development: Access to challenging and rewarding opportunities for professional growth and career advancement.
* Hybrid Work Environment: Benefit from a flexible hybrid work setup that supports productivity and work-life balance.
* Transportation Facilities: Convenient company-provided cab services for pick-up and drop-off.
* Comprehensive Medical Benefits: Attractive medical benefits coverage for employees and their families.
* Cafeteria Benefits: Complimentary lunch facility at the workplace.
* Global Exposure: Gain valuable global exposure and access to diverse learning and development opportunities.

title: Principal, Human Rights, India Lead, Human Rights and Social Impact
description:
**Description**
Join us at the forefront of Amazon's sustainability initiatives to work on environmental and social advancements that support Amazon's long-term worldwide sustainability strategy. At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people who are passionate about making a meaningful impact on communities and the environment while helping shape the future of sustainable business practices.
  
  
The Worldwide Sustainability (WWS) organization capitalizes on Amazon's scale and speed to build a more resilient and sustainable company. We manage our social and environmental impacts globally and drive solutions that enable our customers, businesses, and the world to become more sustainable. Through innovative programs and strategic partnerships, we're creating lasting positive change in the communities where we operate while advancing Amazon's commitment to environmental stewardship and social responsibility.
  
  
Amazon's Human Rights & Social Impact program drives customer trust, business continuity, and sustainable social impact by embedding respect for human rights and the environment throughout Amazon’s entire value chain. We implement company-wide standards and commitments such as our Global Human Rights Principles (GHRP) and Supply Chain Standards (SCS). We seek to continuously improve the tools and processes used in integrating human rights and environmental due diligence across the business.
  
  
We are looking for a Principal leader to manage internal business relationships sitting at the intersection of Amazon’s businesses and the HRSI team. The Principal will lead a small team of Regional Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) in India who provide support to regional business teams as they integrate human rights risk management into their businesses. This leader will support multiple complex relationships across the company, and be tasked to address new business issues as they arise by working with HRSI and legal to translate problems and integrate effective solutions with an eye toward automation, scalability, and efficiency. You will be expected to handle both day-to-day issues and longer term, global, and program-wide strategies and initiatives. The Principal, IN Lead, will be a major player in key program developments across our team, including communicating industry initiatives, and working with external stakeholders to manage Amazon’s growing and diverse supply chain. This person will be responsible for influencing without authority broadly across Amazon.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Lead a team of regional SMEs providing human rights support across the globe to WW Ops business teams
* Coordinate with multiple Amazon businesses and functions across India, as well as third-party human rights service providers and suppliers
* Lead cross functional teams across Amazon business units and support teams to enhance and evolve programs to drive measurable improvements on process efficiency and improvements
* Analyze program data and anecdotes (such as escalation data, audit findings, training data, etc.) to drive decisions, make improvements, spot trends, and create efficiencies
* Partner with tech, data, and science teams across Amazon to identify solutions to automate and scale the program
* Develop and improve project and program management processes, prioritizing ways to leverage technology and automate

World Wide Sustainability values diverse experiences. We encourage all candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (inclusive diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
  
  
**Mentorship & Career Growth**
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
  
  
**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or above in a relevant discipline (e.g. Law, Political Science, Public Policy, Public Affairs, Economic Development)
* Experience in supply chain, commodity, and supplier management in a high volume, global sourcing and operations manufacturing environment with a global supply base of contract manufacturers
* 10+ years’ experience in regulatory compliance, ESG reporting, corporate social responsibility, human rights due diligence, or related fields.
* Extensive years of experience at a senior level, working on human rights, labor rights, multi-stakeholder initiatives, international development, labor rights training, or social responsibility

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree or above in a relevant discipline (e.g. Law, Political Science, Public Policy, Public Affairs, Economic Development)
* Experience in program management, logistics, operations, supply chain, transportation, or a related field
* Experience using lean process improvement, six sigma methodologies, or related performance metrics/process improvements to increase efficiency within processes, forecasting, planning, optimization, or logistics

title: Manager, HUB – Legal Counsel (Employment)
description:
Welcome to Haleon. We’re a purpose-driven, world-class consumer company putting everyday health in the hands of millions. In just three years since our launch, we’ve grown, evolved and are now entering an exciting new chapter – one filled with bold ambitions and enormous opportunity.
  
  
Our trusted portfolio of brands – including Sensodyne®, Panadol®, Advil®, Voltaren®, Theraflu®, Otrivin®, and Centrum® – lead in resilient and growing categories. What sets us apart is our unique blend of deep human understanding and trusted science.
  
  
Now it’s time to fully realise the full potential of our business and our people. We do this through our Win as One strategy. It puts our purpose – to deliver better everyday health with humanity – at the heart of everything we do. It unites us, inspires us, and challenges us to be better every day, driven by our agile, performance-focused culture.
  
  
**Purpose of the Role**
The Manager – Legal Counsel, Employment will provide legal support to Haleon’s Global Employment Legal team, with a focus on global employment contracts, employment policies, multi-country employment law research and employee DSAR support. The role will work closely with Global Employment Legal, HR and local Legal teams to support the development and maintenance of global employment documentation and policies, while ensuring appropriate consideration of local legal requirements.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
Global Employment Contracts & Documentation
  
  

* Lead on legal aspects of the development and maintenance of employment contract, offer letter and related employment documentation templates across Haleon markets.
* Research and analyse relevant local employment law requirements and identify key country-specific requirements or variations.
* Work with Global Employment Legal, local Legal and HR teams to support the review and lead on the drafting and appropriate localization of employment documentation.
* Facilitate periodic updates to employment documentation in response to relevant legal, policy or business changes.

Employment Policies & Global Projects
  
  

* Provide employment law research and legal support for global employment policies, standards and projects.
* Support the review and updating of employment policies, guidance and related materials and lead on the drafting of updates.
* Work with local Legal and HR teams and Outside Counsel to understand relevant country-specific requirements and support appropriate implementation of global initiatives.
* Prepare practical legal research, summaries and comparative analysis where required.

Employment Legal Knowledge & Process Support
  
  

* Develop and maintain employment law templates, precedents, country guidance, research materials and playbooks.
* Monitor relevant employment law developments and support appropriate updates to existing guidance and documentation.
* Contribute to the standardisation and continuous improvement of repeatable employment legal work.
* Provide legal research and project support to the Global Employment Legal team on other employment matters as required.

Employee DSAR Support – As required
  
  

* Provide employment law support on employee Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs), as required, working with Employment Legal, Privacy and HR teams.
* Assist with the review of relevant information from an employment law perspective and identify matters requiring escalation to the appropriate counsel.

Stakeholder & Cross Functional Management:
  
  

* Work collaboratively with Global Employment Legal, local Legal, HR and other relevant stakeholders to support effective delivery of employment legal initiatives.
* Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain local input, resolve queries and support timely completion of assigned work.

**Qualifications & Essential Skills**

* Bachelor of Law (LL.B) or equivalent legal qualification.
* Qualified lawyer with approximately 8–10 years of relevant legal experience.
* Strong experience in employment and labour law, including employment contracts, policies and employment-related advisory work.
* Proven track record of strong legal drafting skills.
* Strong legal research and analysis skills.
* Experience working with HR and Legal stakeholders.
* Ability to research and analyse employment law requirements across different jurisdictions.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.

**Preferred**

* Experience supporting multinational or multi-jurisdictional employment law matters.
* In-house experience within a multinational organisation and/or experience working in a legal shared services or global capability environment.
* Experience developing employment law templates, playbooks, policies or other standardised legal documentation.
* Exposure to employee privacy, DSARs, investigations, employee relations or employment litigation.

**Technical Skills**

* Employment and labour law research and analysis.
* Drafting and review of employment contracts, offer letters and employment policies.
* Multi-jurisdictional legal research and comparative analysis.
* Legal knowledge management and development of templates and playbooks.
* Proficiency in standard legal research and productivity tools.

description:
**Job Description Summary**
GE HealthCare is seeking a senior legal Counsel in the India legal function. The role spans a highly regulated medtech business, a multi-entity structure including a joint venture, and a fast-moving Indian healthcare policy environment.
  
  
GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology, pharmaceutical diagnostics and digital solutions innovator. In India, we operate through a multi-entity structure spanning manufacturing, R&D, sales and service, and a long-standing joint venture, Wipro GE Healthcare.
  
  
We are seeking a seasoned legal leader to join as Senior Legal Counsel – India. The role sits at the intersection of a highly regulated industry, a complex ownership structure and a fast-evolving Indian healthcare policy landscape.
  
  
**Job Description**
**What You Will Do**

* Commercial: Lead legal support for sales, government tenders, service agreements and channel partner arrangements across all business units; support manufacturing and localisation contracts.
* Disputes & Investigations: Own the litigation and arbitration portfolio, panel counsel and spend; lead internal investigations and regulatory inquiries with global Compliance.
* Governance & JV: Advise Indian entity boards under the Companies Act; serve as legal lead on governance and inter-company arrangements; oversee entity compliance.
* Regulatory: Provide authoritative counsel on medical device, pharma diagnostics, AERB, competition, data protection, FEMA, trade, labour and CSR law; anchor the anti-bribery and HCP compliance programme in India.

**What You Bring**

* LL.B. (LL.M. advantageous); enrolled with a State Bar Council.
* 18+ years' post-qualification experience across inhouse legal department of a large multinational and leading law firm.
* Proven track record in complex commercial contracting, high-value disputes and board-level governance advice.
* Deep command of Indian business and regulatory law; medtech, pharma or regulated-industry experience strongly preferred.
* Experience in matrixed global organisations and advising joint ventures; prior team and budget leadership.

Commercially astute. Unshakeable on integrity. Credible with boards, regulators and partners. A clear, concise communicator and a developer of talent.

title: Legal Associate, Commercial Contracts
description:
**About The Opportunity**

* Dodo Payments is a merchant of record operating across multiple jurisdictions. Every merchant, partner, and vendor relationship is documented and must be legally enforceable across multiple countries.
* This role is for a lawyer to own commercial contracts end-to-end and support corporate documentation, working directly with the Head of Legal, Compliance & Partnerships and founders.

**Role & Responsibilities**

* Own commercial contracts from first request to signature: draft, review, and negotiate vendor, partner, service, and data agreements and NDAs.
* Keep standard documentation current, including master services agreement, merchant terms, pricing schedules, privacy policy, and employment agreements, as business and legal requirements evolve.
* Build the contracting toolkit: templates, fallback positions on common clauses, a negotiation playbook, and a contract register showing signed agreements, counterparties, and renewal dates.
* Act as first point of contact on the legal inbox: resolve routine queries and route complex matters.
* Support corporate documentation workstreams, including employee equity documentation, on clearly scoped tasks, with opportunity to take on more as context builds.
* Support trademark matters and legal/entity inputs for security and compliance certifications.
* Coordinate with external counsel in other jurisdictions when contracts or filings require local input.

* 1–2 years post-qualification experience in general corporate or commercial law at an Indian or international law firm, or in-house at a company with significant cross-border operations.
* Strong drafting skills: precise, clean, and readable by non-lawyers.
* Cross-border exposure: comfort with foreign-law contracts and counterparties outside India.
* Breadth over narrow specialization: ability to handle multiple contract types and jurisdictions.
* Judgment to distinguish critical negotiation points from concessions, and to explain the difference succinctly.
* Real interest in how legal work drives business outcomes; ability to see the commercial impact of drafting.

**Preferred**

* Experience in payments, fintech, or SaaS industries.
* Familiarity with contract lifecycle management tools.
* Prior exposure to regulatory compliance or security certifications.

**Benefits & Culture Highlights**

* Health and Accidental insurances.
* Clear growth path based on performance.
* Ownership of a contract portfolio at a multi-jurisdiction payments company early in your career.
* Direct collaboration with founders and the Head of Legal, Compliance & Partnerships.

* Predictable turnaround on contracts, current and version-controlled documentation, accurate contract register, and reduced first-draft time via templates and playbook within 3–6 months.

title: Founder's Office (Deal Desk)
description:
**About The Opportunity**

* This is a lawyer’s seat in the Founder’s Office at Dodo Payments, a merchant of record carrying compliance responsibility for merchants across global markets. The role brings legal and regulatory judgment to decisions on merchant acceptance, categories, and deal terms, especially for edge cases that don’t fit standard templates.
* The Deal Desk is being established to embed compliance into onboarding, escalation, and deboarding decisions alongside product and risk teams, enabling sales to get real-time compliance answers during calls rather than after.
* For the first three months, the role sits in the Founder’s Office to gather cross-functional input from sales, growth, risk, product, and founders before the desk evolves into a structured function under the Compliance team. Work is reviewed and signed off by the Head of Legal, Compliance & Partnerships.

**Role & Responsibilities**

* Join sales and merchant calls to ensure compliance, acceptance, or contract promises are legally deliverable.
* Bring the regulatory compliance perspective to merchant onboarding, escalation, and deboarding meetings alongside product and risk teams.
* Work through edge cases: merchants with novel business models, categories, or markets; propose compliant paths or clear rejections with rationale for sign-off.
* Help define which new merchant categories and customer types can be supported and under what conditions.
* Handle contract-related aspects of deals and day-to-day commercial requests: negotiated merchant terms, partner term updates, vendor onboarding paperwork, etc., using standard legal documentation.
* Maintain the backend pricing table to ensure negotiated terms are accurately recorded and applied.
* Track regulatory and card scheme rule changes relevant to Dodo’s markets and flag operational impacts.
* Convert recurring compliance decisions into written positions to avoid repeated escalations.

**Skills & Qualifications**
**Must-Have**

* Qualified lawyer with 1–2 years post-qualification experience in the general corporate team of an Indian or international law firm, or in an in-house legal team at a company with cross-border operations.
* Comfortable starting without predefined answers or processes.
* Creative problem-solving: understanding rules is the baseline; finding workable paths within them is the core task.
* Clear, fast written communication with non-lawyers (sales, product, partners) to deliver actionable answers.
* Strong spine: desire to close deals but willingness to say no when compliance boundaries are breached, and ability to hold that position under pressure.
* Sound judgment on the limits of authority: decisive on known matters, disciplined about escalating unknowns.
* Interest in payments, cross-border regulation, and how compliance shapes business offerings. Prior payments exposure is a plus, not required.

**Preferred**

* Experience in merchant of record models, card scheme rules, or cross-border payment compliance.

**Benefits & Culture Highlights**

* Health and Accidental insurances.
* Clear growth path based on performance.
* Direct exposure to founders and cross-functional decision-making from day one.
* Hands-on grounding in live cases involving cross-border payments regulation and merchant of record structures.
* Opportunity to build and eventually lead the Compliance Deal Desk as it matures.

Skills: sales,deals,compliance

You will partner with senior leadership, Human Resources, Legal, Employee Relations, Finance, and other functional teams to promote ethical business conduct, strengthen compliance programs, and ensure alignment with RTX policies and applicable laws and regulations. * Investigate alleged violations of applicable laws, regulations, and RTX policies across Collins businesses in India, engaging internal and external resources as required.
* Develop and implement Legal Compliance strategies, programs, and initiatives to identify, prevent, and mitigate compliance risks.

* Support the ongoing development and communication of the RTX Code of Conduct and related compliance communications across India and APAC.
* Manage and provide guidance to the network of Collins Local Ethics & Compliance Officers across India.

* Conduct Conflict of Interest (COI) reviews and escalate cases in accordance with RTX and Collins policies and procedures.
* Review and disposition RTX Global Ethics & Compliance (GEC) Annual Certification variant responses.
* Support compliance requirements arising from government directives, contractual obligations, ESG requirements, and EU sustainability regulations.
* Identify recurring compliance issues and recommend improvements to policies, procedures, and practices.
* Support Speak Up helpline matters and Ethics & Compliance investigations in accordance with established policies and processes.
* Leverage data analytics, scorecards, and risk assessments to monitor compliance trends and support informed decision-making.
* Collaborate with global stakeholders to strengthen compliance governance and ensure consistent implementation of corporate standards.
* Travel as required, approximately 15% of the time.

What You Will Learn
  
  

* Gain exposure to global Ethics & Compliance strategies and governance within a leading aerospace and defense organization.
* Develop expertise in corporate ethics, regulatory compliance, investigations, and risk management.
* Build strong partnerships with senior business leaders and global Legal and GEC teams.
* Strengthen capabilities in compliance program management, stakeholder consultation, and risk mitigation.
* Gain exposure to aerospace and defense contracting requirements, government regulations, and emerging ESG and sustainability obligations.
* Enhance leadership, communication, analytical, and decision-making skills while contributing to a strong culture of integrity.

**Qualifications You Must Have**

* Typically requires a Degree/Master's degree and a minimum of 12+ years of relevant experience in experience working in an international organization in similar role.

**Qualifications We Prefer**

* Strong interpersonal, client consultation and problem-solving skills.
* Proven agility and adaptability to changes in direction in a fast-paced working environment, including ability to flex to support priority initiatives as needed.
* Knowledge of key ethics and compliance risks including Anti-Corruption / Anti-Bribery (ABAC), Privacy, Speak Up helpline, and Ethics & Compliance Investigations.
* Strong written and verbal communications skills.
* Demonstrated success in collaboration and teambuilding.
* Prior experience developing and managing data analytics / visualization tools.
* Experience pulling data from diverse sets into a common tool such as scorecards and risk assessments.
* Preferred Knowledge of, and experience in, aerospace and defense ethics and compliance including the contracting and regulatory environment.

description:
**About Us**
For well over a century, ExxonMobil has been at the heart of creating and growing a modern world. We embrace the power and promise of technology, pushing the boundaries of what's possible. For billions around the world, lives are better and last longer because of the innovative problem solving and reliable energy we provide. And when it comes to developing industrial solutions to reduce carbon emissions, ExxonMobil is truly the leader.
  
  
We don't stop at "good enough." We are committed to doing what's right, even if it's difficult or unpopular. We hold ourselves to high standards, challenge what's possible and invest in innovation to meet society's critical needs.
  
  
Real change begins with bold questions, drive, and ambition. Here, your talent, determination and contributions shape how far you'll go and the impact you'll make along the way.
  
  
Our future success depends on exceptional people. We invest in developing talent through meaningful work, challenging assignments, mentorship, and experiences that help build the next generation of leaders.
  
  
**Our Culture**
We are uniquely ExxonMobil. Integrity, care, excellence, resilience and courage, these core values determine how we work every day. At ExxonMobil, our values aren't just words— they're how we show up, focused on delivering the right answer, the right way, every day.
  
  
What role will you play in the team
  
  
The Buyer / Contracts Manager leads, develops, negotiates and executes contracts for goods and services across one or more procurement categories, including direct and indirect spend. The role ensures full compliance with corporate standards and regional requirements across APAC, Europe, Latin America and North America. It requires strong commercial acumen, legal and contractual awareness, and sound technical understanding of the categories managed, supporting upstream, midstream, downstream and manufacturing operations.
  
  
Working from India with global stakeholders and suppliers, you will use your language skills in Mandarin, Spanish and/or Portuguese to engage global suppliers and business partners.
  
  
What you do
  
  
Drive value, efficiency, and expanded market advantage via end-to-end category management phases, while ensuring operational integrity. Plan, organize and control sourcing activities, negotiations and contracts for the acquisition of goods and services. Develop comprehensive agreements for your categories and associated services for business clients on a timely basis. These agreements ensure all acquisitions are made on competitive terms, optimize total cost, maintain high standards of quality, safety and service, and build strong, reliable supplier relationships.
  
  
Categories in scope
  
  
Experience in one or more of the following categories (or comparable ones) is required:
  
  

* Equipment & Materials
* Craft Labor & Contracted Services:
* Chemicals & Chemical Products
* Engineering & Project Procurement
* Professional Services
* Transport & Logistics:
* Information Technology

Key responsibilities
  
  

* Understand market, industry and business drivers to provide fast, innovative and value-added commercial support to internal clients.
* Set the strategic vision for assigned categories, including supplier identification, evaluation, qualification, sourcing and ongoing supplier relationship management (SRM), to meet global requirements.
* Evaluate global suppliers and emerging players in APAC, Europe, Latin America and North America to support strategic sourcing decisions, including low-cost-country sourcing where appropriate.
* Own commercial actions and drive business value through RFx, bids, renewals and amendments with a focus on total cost of ownership (TCO). Negotiate medium- to high-complexity contracts, and draft or review Statements of Work, Master Service Agreements, Global Supply Agreements, rate schedules and other vendor contracts together with internal and vendor legal teams.
* Manage the end-to-end contract lifecycle, including award, mobilization, performance and KPI/SLA tracking, change orders, claims, renewal and close-out.
* Spend management: analyze spend and patterns to find opportunities for consolidation, supplier base rationalization, demand management, specification optimization and alternatives analysis.
* Monitor global markets to anticipate price changes (including index-linked mechanisms), supply disruptions, capacity constraints and technological changes.
* Communicate and collaborate proactively with Projects/Operations, Business Lines, functions (Legal, Finance/Controllers, HSE, Quality, Tax) and other procurement category teams to maximize commercial outcomes.
* Ensure all contracts meet regulatory, trade, labor, HSE, sustainability/ESG and compliance standards in each region, including anti-bribery, sanctions and export control.
* Ensure all documents and exhibits are complete and included in the final contract, and that all functional reviews and management approvals are completed or obtained as required.
* Handle Procure-to-Pay (P2P) activities and contract lifecycle management for assigned projects and categories, working with relevant partners across the organization.
* Bring industry expertise to category strategies that deliver savings, risk mitigation and business transformation.

**Required Qualifications And Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering / supply chain, Business or a related experience, with a minimum CGPA of 6.0 or equivalent
* Minimum 02 years of experience in procurement, contracts management or strategic sourcing, preferably in Oil & Gas, Power, Petrochemicals, Chemical Manufacturing, EPC or a similar industry.
* Proven experience managing global contracts and working across regions (APAC, Europe, Americas).
* Technical understanding of the categories managed, such as product specifications and manufacturing processes, labor productivity and rate structures, or chemical properties, handling and regulatory requirements.
* Knowledge of international trade, Incoterms, customs and logistics.
* Analytical skills and knowledge of TCO/TSC principles, cost modelling and should-cost analysis.
* Knowledge of the P2P process and ERP/e-sourcing systems (e.g., SAP, Ariba, Coupa).

Language requirements
  
  

* English: full professional proficiency, written and spoken (mandatory).
* Plus professional working proficiency in at least one of: Mandarin Chinese, Spanish or Portuguese. Ability to negotiate, review commercial documents and correspond with suppliers in that language. Proficiency in more than one is an added advantage.
* Recognized language certification (e.g., HSK, DELE, CELPE-Bras) or equivalent professional experience is preferred.

Skills and attributes
  
  

* Effective negotiation, advocacy and influencing skills
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
* Ability to work across cultures, time zones and organizations
* General industry and global market knowledge
* Fast learner, results- and customer-oriented
* Willingness to travel 5–10%

title: Insurance Manager
description:
**About The Role**
We are looking for an Insurance professional with 5–10 years of experience to lead the procurement and management of
**project insurance**
and
**construction insurance**
programmes for the company’s high-
**capex**
infrastructure projects, including GPU clusters,
**data centres**
, and associated power and cooling assets. The role will work closely with brokers, insurers, lenders, and project teams to secure bankable, cost-effective cover from construction through operations. Internally, the position will be part of the CFO organisation, working closely with senior management to ensure alignment with
**lender compliance**
requirements and
**APAC insurance**
market dynamics. The role also demands deep understanding of
**data center risk**
profiles and the ability to structure coverage that meets complex project finance and operational needs across jurisdictions.
  
  
The role is ideal for someone with strong
**insurance placement**
, contract review, and stakeholder management capabilities who wants exposure to
**project finance**
,
**lender requirements**
, and senior leadership interactions in a fast-growing environment.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
**Insurance Procurement & Placement**

* Procure and place project insurance programmes including construction / erection all risks, delay in start-up, marine cargo and transit, operational property damage and business interruption, and third-party liability, ensuring alignment with lender compliance and APAC insurance regulatory frameworks.
* Run broker and insurer selection, including RFPs, market sounding, quote comparison, and negotiation of terms, pricing, and deductibles—leveraging relationships with London/Lloyd’s and Asia insurance hubs for optimal coverage and pricing across APAC jurisdictions.
* Prepare underwriting submissions and risk information, including sums-insured and loss-of-profit assessments, in coordination with project, technical, and finance teams—ensuring robust risk transfer for capex projects.
* Place cover for specialist risks such as equipment breakdown, cyber, technology E&O, and political risk across APAC, incorporating data center risk considerations and lender compliance standards.
* Track renewals, premium payments, endorsements, and claims; maintain the insurance register and ensure full traceability for project finance due diligence and lender compliance reporting.

**Lender & Contract Compliance**

* Align insurance programmes with lender requirements under financing documents, including insurance covenants, loss payee and co-insured arrangements, and cancellation notice provisions—ensuring full lender compliance for capex projects.
* Coordinate with lenders’ insurance advisors and provide certificates, reports, and compliance confirmations during financing and thereafter—supporting timely drawdowns and ongoing covenant adherence.
* Review insurance and indemnity clauses in supply, colocation, customer, and lease contracts, and advise on risk allocation—ensuring alignment with APAC insurance best practices and project insurance standards.
* Coordinate contractor-procured and company-procured policies to avoid gaps and overlaps in cover, particularly for data center risk and high-value technology assets.

**Risk Assessment & Claims**

* Work with technical advisors and project teams to identify and quantify project and operational risks—including data center risk, GPU cluster exposure, and infrastructure resilience—and support risk transfer decisions for capex projects.
* Support risk engineering and loss-control surveys and track implementation of recommendations to mitigate exposure across construction and operational phases.
* Manage claims end to end, including notification, engagement of loss adjusters, documentation, and recovery follow-up—ensuring minimal business interruption for data centres and power infrastructure.

**Reporting & Strategic Support**

* Build insurance cost estimates and budgets for project financial models, investor presentations, and lender discussions—ensuring transparency and realism in capex planning.
* Provide insurance inputs for financing term sheets, information memorandums, and due diligence requests—ensuring comprehensive risk disclosure for APAC insurance and project insurance structures.
* Develop insurance policies, guidelines, and a group-wide programme as the business scales across geographies—ensuring consistency with lender compliance and APAC regulatory expectations.

**Candidate Profile**
**Experience**

* 5–10 years of experience in:
* Project or construction insurance broking—with hands-on involvement in capex projects and data centre risk assessment.
* Corporate insurance or risk management for infrastructure, energy, or real asset companies—particularly in APAC or multinational contexts.
* Property, engineering, or construction underwriting—with exposure to delay in start-up, erection all risks, and business interruption coverage.
* Insurance advisory for project finance transactions (e.g., as a lenders’ insurance advisor)—ensuring lender compliance and robust risk transfer structures.

**Educational Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Insurance, Risk Management, Engineering, or related field—additional certifications (e.g., CPCU, CRMP, PRM) preferred.

**Technical Skills**

* Hands-on experience procuring insurance for large capex projects across construction and operational phases—especially for data centres, GPU clusters, and power infrastructure.
* Ability to read and negotiate policy wordings, endorsements, and contractual insurance clauses—including APAC insurance market conventions and lender compliance requirements.
* Working knowledge of sums-insured, PML / MFL, loss-of-profit assessment, and data center risk quantification methodologies.
* Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint—especially for financial modeling, insurance cost analysis, and investor-grade reporting.

**Soft Skills**

* Strong negotiation, communication, and presentation skills—especially when interfacing with lenders, investors, and technical stakeholders.
* High attention to detail and follow-through on policies, renewals, and lender compliance documentation.
* Ability to work in fast-paced and entrepreneurial environments—balancing multiple capex projects across APAC.
* Strong ownership mindset and ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously—ensuring seamless coordination between project teams, brokers, and insurers.

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience placing insurance for data centres, digital infrastructure, power, or renewable energy projects—especially with GPU clusters and high-density computing assets.
* Experience with high-value technology and IT equipment cover, including GPU or similar assets—understanding of technology E&O and equipment breakdown exposures.
* Experience with international insurance markets (London / Lloyd’s, Asia hubs) and APAC regulatory regimes—including cross-border policy structuring and lender compliance alignment.
* Exposure to lender insurance requirements and project finance due diligence—including preparation of insurance schedules for term sheets and financing close.

**What The Role Offers**

* Direct exposure to senior leadership, lenders, and investors—playing a pivotal role in project finance and capex strategy.
* Ownership of insurance across high-impact, multi-country infrastructure projects—especially in APAC and for data center risk mitigation.
* Broad exposure across project finance, risk management, and contract negotiation—with a focus on lender compliance and APAC insurance best practices.
* Fast learning curve in a high-growth environment—building expertise in construction insurance, data center risk, and capex project risk transfer strategies.

You will lead North America compliance efforts across complex, multi-jurisdictional EPR regulatory landscapes — spanning waste streams including packaging, electronics, batteries, and textiles. Regulatory Strategy & Compliance

* Optimize operational costs associated with take-back services, including reverse logistics and recycling processes, through process improvements and strategic partnerships

title: Associate Director, Capital Risk Oversight (Bangalore)
description:
**Job Summary**

* The Capital Risk Oversight team reports into the Treasury CRO, in Enterprise Risk Management. The team’s mandate is to provide assurance to senior management and the Group regulator (Prudential Regulation Authority and Bank of England) on issues that could impact the Group’s regulatory capital position in a BAU environment and across the stress continuum. Areas of responsibility span across a variety of different regulatory submissions and touch on all principal risk types.
* The team provides second line review and challenge on all regulatory stress tests and recovery plans across the SC Group and Solo, HK & SG. The team is a dedicated second line function for the development of Treasury risk related Resolvability capabilities and provides holistic oversight across all Resolvability capabilities.
* The team provides ongoing review and challenge for capital planning purposes to ensure that capital metrics are managed within Risk Appetite and that any distribution plans are credible and affordable under plausible downside stress scenarios.

**Key Responsibilities**
**Stress Testing Oversight and Challenge**

* Support independent 2LOD oversight of regulatory and internal stress tests, including ICAAP, BCST, RPST, RST, climate stress tests, Management Stress Tests and relevant material legal entity exercises.
* Provide SME reviews on Treasury risk results, including the evolution of income and balance sheet amounts, including the determination of key judgements embedded therein.
* Challenge scenarios, methodologies, assumptions, judgments, results and management actions, ensuring outcomes appropriately reflect the scenario, risk profile and legal-entity dynamics.
* Provide independent conclusions on capital resilience, recovery capacity and material vulnerabilities, including the adequacy of remediation against regulatory, audit and 2LOD findings.

**Stress Testing Analytics**

* Provide analytical support to the team in summarising and reviewing the SBAP outputs, model results, overlays, management adjustments and key assumptions.
* Challenge model-use testing, data quality, reconciliations and in-house analytical controls to ensure outputs are complete, reliable and decision-useful.
* Explore automation opportunities in review and challenge of the results and dashboards for management information.

**Consolidation of second line Assurance and Governance**

* Consolidate input from Treasury Risk and other Risk Framework Owners into an integrated 2LOD assurance view.
* Assess compliance with applicable policies, standards, regulatory requirements, controls, attestations and approved dispensations.
* Produce formal assurance reporting for GRC and BRC, clearly escalating material observations, residual risks and unresolved actions.

**Recovery Planning and Management Actions Oversight**

* Support independent review and challenge of Recovery Plan Stress Tests, recovery scenarios and the associated management-action framework.
* Assess the credibility, quantification, timing, dependencies and execution constraints of management actions.
* Provide independent conclusions on total recovery capacity and the Group’s ability to restore capital and liquidity resilience.

**Policy Governance and Risk Frameworks**

* Maintain oversight of Treasury Capital Risk policies and supporting governance frameworks.
* Lead policy effectiveness reviews and challenge policy compliance across Treasury risk activities.
* Review horizon scanning of regulatory developments and assess impacts on capital and resolution frameworks.
* Manage policy dispensations, exceptions and remediation activities.
* Ensure policies remain aligned with regulatory expectations and enterprise risk management framework.

**Management of Process Universe and Control ownership**

* Act as SME for Capital Risk Oversight and stress-testing process architecture within Process Universe and ARIS.
* Define 2LOD processes, responsibilities, handoffs and dependencies, maintaining clear separation from first-line ownership and specialist validation.
* Drive improvements to process controls, operating models, governance, documentation and management information.

**Skills And Experience**
**Must-have Skills**

* Stress Testing and Scenario Analytics
* Risk Analysis and Analytical Support
* Policy Management and Monitoring

**Other Skills**

* Data Analytics
* Report writing
* Governance, Oversight and Control

**Qualifications**

* Prior experience in Stress Testing, Market Risk, Credit Risk, Operational Risk, ICAAP, Regulatory capital requirements etc.
* Good understanding of Financial, Risk and Capital metrics
* Language: Proficiency in verbal & written English

**Competencies**
Action Oriented
  
  
Collaborates
  
  
Customer Focus
  
  
Gives Clarity & Guidance
  
  
Manages Ambiguity
  
  
Develops Talent

Nimble Learning
  
  
Decision Quality
  
  
Courage

Strategic Mindset

title: Sr Attorney
description:
**Job Description**
The Senior Attorney will work as part of a team of regional legal and compliance subject matter experts and will be expected to translate global compliance expectations into practical, locally relevant guidance. The role includes the following responsibilities:
  
  

* Lead regional anticorruption and fraud risk assessments and use the results to prioritize prevention, detection, and remediation activities.
* Provide timely, practical advice on anticorruption, antibribery, conflicts of interest, gifts and hospitality, charitable donations, sponsorships, travel, third-party engagements, and government interactions.

* Evaluate internal and external compliance trends, enforcement developments, audit findings, and hotline data to identify emerging risks and program improvement opportunities.

The role requires strong familiarity with international anticorruption laws and standards, including the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, the UK Bribery Act, and related books-and-records and internal-controls expectations. Experience with investigations, third-party risk management, compliance program assessment, and remediation is essential.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Key Responsibilities**

* Assess legal, regulatory, reputational, and operational compliance risks and recommend practical mitigation steps.
* Advise and influence senior business leaders on anticorruption, fraud, and integrity compliance matters.
* Lead cross-functional compliance initiatives, including training, monitoring, control enhancements, and remediation.
* Develop, improve, and standardize processes that support a risk-based compliance program.
* Serve as a trusted advisor and change leader who promotes ethical decision-making and accountability.
* Manage investigations, external counsel, and related budgets efficiently and effectively.
* Identify emerging risks from enforcement trends, business changes, audits, investigations, and data analytics.

* Juris Doctor, equivalent non-U.S. law degree, or comparable legal training strongly preferred.

* Strong initiative, ownership mindset, and ability to drive priorities independently.
* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, communication, and project management skills.

title: Company Secretary
description:
**About The Role**
We are looking for a qualified and detail-oriented
**Company Secretary (CS)**
with 3–5 years of experience in corporate compliance, legal governance, and company secretarial practices. The ideal candidate should have experience working with startups or high-growth organizations, along with exposure to
**pre-IPO readiness, IPO-related activities, and post-IPO compliance**
.

* Ensure compliance with the Companies Act, 2013, applicable SEBI regulations, and other relevant corporate laws.

* Support pre-IPO readiness, including compliance reviews, legal due diligence, documentation, and identification of compliance gaps.

* Organize Board Meetings, Committee Meetings, Annual General Meetings (AGMs), and Extraordinary General Meetings (EGMs).
* Prepare meeting notices, agendas, minutes, resolutions, and supporting documents.
* Coordinate with directors and senior management to ensure compliance with meeting and governance requirements.
* Manage corporate actions relating to share transfers, share capital changes, ESOPs, and fundraising, as applicable.

* Draft, review, and maintain corporate and secretarial documents.
* Coordinate with external legal counsel, auditors, investors, and regulatory authorities on compliance-related matters.
* Maintain compliance calendars and ensure accurate documentation and timely reporting.
* Support the development of internal compliance processes and governance policies suitable for a growing organization.

**Required Qualifications And Experience**

* Qualified Company Secretary (CS) and member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI).

* Experience working with startups, high-growth companies, or organizations preparing for an IPO.
* Exposure to pre-IPO preparation, IPO-related documentation, or post-IPO compliance is strongly preferred.
* Good knowledge of the Companies Act, 2013, MCA/ROC filings, SEBI regulations, and corporate governance practices.
* Strong drafting, documentation, organizational, and stakeholder management skills.
* Ability to work independently, manage multiple deadlines, and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.

title: Legal/ Corporate Compliance Operations Associate
description:
Who we are
  
  
**About Stripe**
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
  
  
**About The Team**
Stripe's global legal operations team is dedicated to delivering an exceptional support experience for legal entities, law firms, and government agencies reporting compliance violations and policy non-adherence. The team plays a vital role in managing and ensuring compliance with various legal requests and requirements that Stripe users must regularly follow.
  
  
What You’ll Do Stripe is launching Stripe Delivery Centers - a global team to design, implement and grow Stripe’s operations for the next decade. We are looking for dynamic and curious people that have a passion for solving global user issues, building operations, driving process improvements and want to play a front-line role in building this new operational capability for Stripe and accelerating Stripe’s growth. If you like challenging, scaled problems and are interested in helping users feel secure and supported while they navigate their complaints - let us know!
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Review and validate reports of violations flagged by various agencies while ensuring compliance to law and regulatory board.
* Support users' concerns and provide exceptional customer service.
* Analyze current processes and initiate changes aimed at scaling operations and enhancing user experience.
* Respond to reports submitted by legal and government entities via email.
* Collaborate closely with other Stripe teams to enhance product offerings and improve messaging around new products and features.
* Gather unique insights into how thousands of businesses using Stripe operate and scale.
* Gain a comprehensive understanding of Stripe's operations from the ground up and contribute to the organization's future impact.
* Play a key role in establishing a new team and fostering an operational culture at Stripe.
* Partner with global operations specialists or business process owners to manage critical workflows effectively.

Who You Are
  
  
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
  
  
**Minimum Requirements**

* You have a user first mindset and are energized by the challenge of solving difficult problems
* You have 2 - 4 yrs of experience in customer support and technical support.
* You have excellent communication skills, both written and verbally
* You excel in critical thinking and problem solving
* You might have close to 2 to 6 years of experience in customer service or internal/external user-facing operations
* You enjoy learning about products and processes, you are an organized, self-starter with passion for finding solutions to our user’s challenges
* You are able to identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency
* You have a process-oriented mindset and ability to get things done
* You enjoy working in an in-office environment with strong cross team collaboration and support
* You are able to prioritize and enjoy working in a dynamic space
* You are humble and have a proven track record for working well across teams and with external partners

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior experience or knowledge in user support
* Prior experience in troubleshooting
* Prior experience working on projects or process improvement initiatives

In-office expectations
  
  
Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.
  
  
Pay and benefits
  
  
Stripe does not yet include pay ranges in job postings in every country. Stripe strongly values pay transparency and is working toward pay transparency globally.
  
  
We look forward to hearing from you.
  
  
At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.
  
  
Apply now

**Job Description: Senior Product Regulatory Compliance Analyst**
The Senior Product Regulatory Compliance Analyst supports Fluke's global product regulatory compliance operating model by leading the monitoring of regulatory compliance developments, assessing product impacts, coordinating cross-functional compliance work, and maintaining audit-ready compliance documentation. The role helps move compliance activities upstream to strengthen Fluke’s ability to identify, scope and action upcoming global regulatory changes proactively to avoid unplanned shipment and revenue impacts and help drive improvements to the global compliance roadmap process and systems. This role partners with Product Safety and Product Environmental Compliance, Engineering, Product Management, Supply Chain, Quality, Legal, and external certification bodies to translate regulatory and standards-based requirements into practical business actions.

* Lead the Global Regulatory Roadmap process by monitoring emerging and changing global product regulations and standards that may affect Fluke products incl. packaging, batteries, product safety, software-enabled products, hazardous-location products, environmental reporting obligations, and market-access requirements, amongst others.
* Perform applicability and impact assessments, translating regulatory requirements into business actions, due dates, required evidence, risks, owners, and escalation items.
* Maintain project plans, milestone trackers, risk logs, evidence trackers, regulatory due-date summaries, revenue-impact inputs, and leadership status updates.
* Coordinate activities with Design Engineering, Sustaining Engineering, Product Management, Supply Chain, Quality, Legal, Product Safety and Environmental Compliance, and third-party certification bodies.
* Lead and support compliance projects for requirements such as EU Battery Regulation, RoHS, REACH/PFAS, PPWR, EPR, BIS, EUDR, product safety certification, and related global product requirements.
* Lead and support continuous improvement efforts incl. current-state and future-state process mapping, standard work, RACI models, standard work, KPI dashboards, visual management tools, and other improvements to the integrated compliance operating model.
* Play a key role in developing Fluke’s usage and integration of systems and data bases to support regulatory compliance monitoring and early detection, assessment, processing, tracking, and reporting.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, regulatory affairs, environmental science, quality, supply chain, or a related technical or business field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 10+ years of experience supporting product compliance, regulatory affairs, certification, environmental compliance, supplier evidence collection, or technical program/project management.
* Proven ability to interpret regulatory or standards-based requirements and convert them into practical project tasks, evidence requirements, risk summaries, and stakeholder actions.
* Strong written communication skills, including concise compliance summaries, status updates, declarations, audit documentation, and customer-facing responses.
* Strong Excel, data organization, dashboarding, project tracking, and documentation-management skills.

Help a global pharmaceutical company adopt new technology, including AI, safely. You will work with project teams, vendors and quality colleagues across the US, Europe, Japan and India, and help shape how Astellas secures emerging technology such as AI.

Scope: Third-party and cloud (SaaS) solutions, in-house built applications and AI systems (models, agents, copilots), for both GxP (FDA/EU-regulated) and non-regulated use.
  
  

* Plan & Design: Join new projects early to identify security and compliance risks; assess vendors and cloud services before contracts are signed (e.g., SOC 2 reports, ISO 27001 certifications, security questionnaires); make sure contracts include the right security terms; and assess risks in new AI tools with our AI Security team.
* Requirements & Standards: Own the security requirements in Astellas' System Life Cycle (SLC), our process for delivering and validating systems, keeping them clear, testable and tied to policy and regulation (e.g., 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11); keep security standards current as policies, threats and technologies such as AI evolve; and tailor requirements to each system's type and risk.
* Build & Change: Review specifications, designs and test evidence to confirm security requirements are met before go-live and with every change; provide the security sign-off at key project checkpoints and in change control; and drive gaps to resolution or manage formal, time-limited exceptions.
* Operate & Monitor: Run periodic reviews of live systems and reassess key vendors; track open risks and exceptions through to closure; maintain the technology risk register and report on risk to leadership; run and improve risk and vendor-risk workflows in OneTrust; and, when systems or vendor relationships end, confirm access is removed and data is returned or destroyed.
* Partnership & Governance: Act as Cybersecurity's partner to our IT quality and compliance team, keeping security and quality requirements aligned and free of duplication, including for AI systems; guide and train system owners, project teams and vendors; support audits and assessments with evidence; and work with procurement, legal and quality colleagues across regions.

**Required Qualification**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity or a related field.
* 5+ years in cybersecurity compliance, IT risk or third-party risk management.
* Hands-on experience defining or reviewing security requirements for systems throughout their life cycle.
* Hands-on experience assessing the security of vendors and cloud services.
* Working knowledge of common security frameworks such as NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53 and ISO 27001.
* Strong written English and the ability to explain findings clearly to technical and business audiences across time zones.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in a GxP-regulated environment (computer system validation, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, GAMP 5), including validation documents such as user requirements, specifications and traceability matrices.
* Experience with OneTrust (IT and third-party risk modules), ALM (requirements management) or Veeva Vault.
* Exposure to AI risk assessment and cloud/SaaS security.
* Knowledge of secure development (NIST SSDF) and supply chain risk (NIST SP 800-161) guidance.
* Certifications such as CRISC, CISA, CISM, CISSP, CCSP or CTPRP.

**Working Environment**
At Astellas we recognize the importance of work/life balance, and we are proud to offer a hybrid working solution allowing time to connect with colleagues at the office with the flexibility to also work from home. We believe this will optimize the most productive work environment for all employees to succeed and deliver. Hybrid work from certain locations may be permitted in accordance with Astellas’ Responsible Flexibility

title: Audit and Compliance Specialist
description:
**Overview**
**JOB DESCRIPTION: Audit and Compliance Specialist - Governance, Risk & Compliance**

* JOB IDENTIFICATION

**APTEAN JOB TABLE: Information Security**
**APTEAN JOB LEVEL: B**
**APTEAN JOB TITLE: Audit and Compliance Specialist - Governance, Risk & Compliance**
**REPORTS TO**
Full line: Director, Information Security
  
  
Dotted line: Lead Audit and Compliance Specialist
  
  

* GENERAL JOB SUMMARY

The Audit and Compliance Specialist - Governance, Risk & Compliance performs the assurance activities of the Aptean Information Security Office: testing whether security controls are designed adequately and operating effectively, producing the evidence that demonstrates it, and assessing third parties, products and AI systems against Aptean control requirements. The role supports external audits and certification assessments, coordinates technical security assessments, authors security policies, standards and department handbooks, and administers the exception and control registers.
  
  

* SCOPE

**Knowledge**
Possesses extensive experience and deep expertise in the field. Effectively resolves a broad range of challenges using sound judgment, creativity, and practical knowledge. Recognized as a fully proficient professional who can operate independently within their area of specialization.
  
  
**Complexity**
Manages diverse and complex assignments that require thorough analysis and evaluation of multiple factors. Demonstrates strong decision-making skills in selecting appropriate methods, techniques, and solutions. Regularly collaborates and builds relationships with senior internal and external stakeholders.
  
  
**Supervision**
Works with a high degree of autonomy and receives minimal day-to-day supervision. Typically requires only general direction for new or unique assignments while independently managing routine responsibilities.
  
  

* ORGANIZATION

**Full Line**

* Director, Information Security

**Dotted Line**

* Lead Audit and Compliance Specialist
* PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
* Executes control testing against the information security control framework on the defined cycle, including sampling, test procedures and documented conclusions on operating effectiveness.
* Assesses control evidence for sufficiency, records findings with severity, root cause and accountable owner, and validates remediation evidence before closing findings raised by the function.
* Supports external audits, certification assessments and customer-driven assessments through evidence preparation, request tracking, auditor liaison and follow-up submissions.
* Coordinates technical security assessments: defines scope against control, certification and contractual requirements, manages independent assessors, reviews deliverable quality, and registers resulting findings for tracking.
* Conducts pre-engagement and periodic third-party security and privacy due diligence assessments, reviews vendor assurance artefacts and contractual security requirements, and issues documented risk opinions.
* Assesses AI systems against applicable security control requirements, performs AI audit and assurance activity, and provides security input to AI risk categorisation and operator role determination undertaken by the governance function.
* Drafts and maintains security policies, standards and department security handbooks, working with subject matter experts to define applicable controls, expected evidence and accountable owners.
* Administers the exception and risk registers, monitors expiry, produces recurring compliance and control reporting for management and governance committees, and performs other related duties as assigned.
* JOB SPECIFICATIONS

Education
  
  
**Preferred Required**
**Required Preferred Degree/Certification**
☒ ☐ Bachelor’s degree
  
  
☐ ☐ Master’s degree
  
  
☐ ☐ Ph.D.
  
  
☐ ☐ J.D. (law)
  
  
☐ ☒ Certification: ISO 27001 Lead Auditor/Lead Implementer, CISA, CCSK
  
  
☐ ☐ Registration
  
  
☐ ☐ Licensure:
  
  
☐ ☐ Other
  
  
**Work Experience**
4 years of experience in information security in a dedicated governance, risk and compliance, security compliance or IT audit role.
  
  
**Knowledge**

* Information security control frameworks - SOC1, SOC 2, SOC3, ISO 27001, ISO 42001 and NIST 800-53 or NIST CSF - including control interpretation and evidence requirements.
* Audit and assessment practice, including sampling, evidence sufficiency, finding classification and corrective action tracking.
* Third-party and vendor security risk assessment methodology, contractual security requirements and assurance artefact review.
* Artificial intelligence governance and AI security requirements, including risk-tiering under the EU AI Act, operator role concepts, ISO 42001, and how AI systems are assessed against security controls.
* Security documentation hierarchy - how policy, standards, baselines, procedures and department handbooks relate to one another.
* Cloud security concepts across at least one major provider, sufficient to interpret cloud control requirements and assess supporting evidence.
* Data protection principles and regulatory obligations, including GDPR and privacy assessment processes.

**Skills And Abilities**

* Writes clearly and precisely in English. A substantial part of the role produces documentation that non-security teams must follow and auditors must rely on; writing ability is assessed during selection.
* Reaches supportable conclusions from incomplete evidence, and states limitations rather than overstating assurance.
* Distinguishes an isolated control failure from a systemic control weakness and escalates accordingly.
* Scopes, commissions and challenges assessments delivered by specialist third parties without performing the technical work.
* Works effectively with technical teams without owning their work - asks precise questions, obtains attributable answers, and escalates where accountability is declined.
* Manages concurrent assurance activities against defined cycles and reports slippage when it occurs rather than at the milestone date.
* Maintains accuracy and traceability in registers, evidence records and reporting.
* Applies professional scepticism and maintains an independent position under commercial or delivery pressure.

**DISCLAIMER**
*The preceding job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job.*
