title: IT Security Associate - Governance, Compliance and Risk
description:
**Position**
IT Security Associate - Governance, Compliance and Risk
  
  
**Job Description**
About the Role
  
  
Arrow Electronics is looking for a Governance, Risk and Compliance apprentice to join our IT Risk and Governance team in India. This role is built specifically for a student who has completed a university degree and who wants to learn how information security governance actually works inside a global technology distributor, rather than only in a textbook. You will sit with the team that owns Arrow's security certifications, risk framework and compliance programs, and you will contribute to live work from your first month.
  
  
We do not expect you to arrive knowing our frameworks. We expect curiosity, care with detail, and the willingness to ask questions in a room full of experienced practitioners. Everything else is taught, and your schedule is designed around your coursework and examinations.
  
  
**About The Team**
IT Risk and Governance is part of Arrow's Enterprise Security Services organization. The team maintains the Information Security Risk Management Framework, owns the security policy and standards library, runs third-party and vendor risk assessments, and delivers the certification programs that Arrow's customers and contracts depend on. Our current portfolio includes the global ISO 27001 certification program spanning the Americas, EMEA and APAC, CMMC Level 2 readiness for our aerospace and defense business, TISAX assessments for automotive customers, and the consolidation of our GRC tooling onto a single platform.
  
  
The team is deliberately small and global. Members include information security architects, IT compliance analysts, a data security analyst and project managers, working across US, EMEA and APAC time zones. The apprentice reports to the Director, IT Risk and Governance and works day to day alongside a compliance analyst and a security architect.
  
  
What You Will Work On
  
  
The work is real and it changes with the program calendar. Over the course of the apprenticeship you can expect to contribute to several of the following.
  
  

* Evidence collection and tracking for the global ISO 27001 certification program, including chasing outstanding artefacts from control owners and keeping the evidence register current.
* Support for CMMC Level 2 readiness activities, such as maintaining control status trackers and helping assemble documentation packages ahead of assessment milestones.
* Third-party and vendor risk assessments: reviewing questionnaire responses against our Vendor Risk Assessment Standard and flagging gaps for an analyst to validate.
* Migration and data quality work as we consolidate our GRC tooling onto a unified platform, including mapping controls between frameworks and cleaning up legacy records.
* Maintenance of the security policy and standards governance library, including formatting, version control and tracking annual review dates.
* Preparation of recurring reporting, including program status summaries and metrics that go to security leadership.

Key Responsibilities
  
  

* Keep assigned trackers, registers and evidence repositories accurate and current, and raise items that are slipping before they become escalations.
* Draft clear, concise summaries of findings and status for review by an analyst, architect or the director.
* Follow up with control owners and other stakeholders across Arrow to request evidence, clarify responses and confirm closure of open items.
* Compare documentation and questionnaire responses against published Arrow standards and applicable control frameworks, and record where they do not line up.
* Handle confidential and restricted information with the discretion the classification requires, and complete all assigned security training on time.
* Attend program stand-ups and take accurate notes, actions and owners.
* Ask when something is unclear rather than guessing, and tell your mentor early when coursework will affect your availability.

What You Will Learn
  
  
This apprenticeship is structured as a learning path, not an administrative placement. By the end of twelve months a successful apprentice should be able to do the following.
  
  

* Explain how an ISO 27001 certification cycle runs end to end, from scoping and evidence to external audit and corrective action.
* Read a control framework such as ISO 27001 Annex A or NIST SP 800-171 and trace a requirement to the evidence that satisfies it.
* Run the first pass of a vendor risk assessment against a published standard.
* Work confidently inside a GRC platform, including control mapping, task assignment and reporting.
* Write for a security leadership audience: short, factual, and clear about what changed and what needs a decision.

Who We Are Looking For
  
  
**Required**

* Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program at a recognized university in India, with at least one academic year remaining at the start of the apprenticeship.
* Studying a relevant field such as information technology, computer science, cyber security, information systems, engineering, commerce, law or business administration. We hire for aptitude, not for a single degree.
* Strong written and spoken English, since most of the team and its stakeholders are outside India.
* Comfortable with Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and Teams, and willing to learn new tools quickly.
* Genuinely careful with detail. Much of this work is the difference between an assessment that passes and one that does not.
* Available for the agreed weekly hours and able to overlap with colleagues in EMEA and the United States for part of the week.

**Preferred**

* Coursework, certification study or project work touching information security, audit, risk management or data privacy.
* Familiarity with any control framework or standard, including ISO 27001, NIST, SOC 2, PCI DSS or GDPR, at an introductory level.
* Exposure to a GRC, ticketing or project tracking platform, or to basic data handling in Excel or Power BI.
* Student leadership, campus club, hackathon or volunteer experience that shows follow-through.
* An interest in continuing in security governance after graduation. Strong apprentices are our first consideration for entry-level openings on the team.

**What’s In For You**

* On the job skill-based training, projects, assignments, opportunity to learn new skills.
* Annual Fixed Stipend (INR 30,000 per month)
* Insurance (Self):

+ Medical : Coverage of INR 500,000/-
+ Accidental & Life as per policy

* Time off:
* 20 days of Annual leave
* 12 days of Casual/Sick leave &
* 10 days of Holidays (Festival & National)

**About Arrow**
Arrow Electronics, Inc. (NYSE: ARW), an award-winning Fortune 148 and one of Fortune Magazine’s Most Admired Companies. Arrow guides innovation forward for over 220,000 leading technology manufacturers and service providers. With 2025 sales of USD $30.9 billion, Arrow develops technology solutions that improve business and daily life. Our broad portfolio that spans the entire technology landscape helps customers create, make and manage forward-thinking products that make the benefits of technology accessible to as many people as possible. Learn more at www.arrow.com.
  
  
Our strategic direction of guiding innovation forward is expressed as Five Years Out, a way of thinking about the tangible future to bridge the gap between what's possible and the practical technologies to make it happen. Learn more at https://www.fiveyearsout.com/.
  
  
**Location:**
IN-KA-Bangalore, India (SKAV Seethalakshmi) GESC
  
  
**Time Type**
Full time
  
  
**Job Category**
Business Support

title: Practicing Advocate
description:
⚖️
**HIRING: CORE LITIGATION ADVOCATE | BENGALURU | EXCLUSIVE PROFESSIONAL ENGAGEMENT**

**Jurisiti Legal LLP, a Delhi-based litigation law firm, is looking to engage an experienced Core Litigation Advocate in Bengaluru to lead and manage the firm's litigation matters across the region.**

We are expanding our regional presence and seeking a capable litigation professional who can independently handle court proceedings, develop effective case strategies, manage end-to-end litigation responsibilities, and represent the firm's professional interests within the agreed scope of engagement.

We are looking for someone who combines strong legal knowledge with practical courtroom experience, independent thinking, strategic judgment, professional discipline, and a commitment to delivering high-quality legal work.

With a team of
**12+ in-house advocates and a wider professional network**
, we aim to build a dependable regional litigation practice through long-term professional associations with capable advocates.

🔹 POSITION DETAILS

📍
**Location:**
Bengaluru, Karnataka

⚖️
**Position:**
Core Litigation Advocate

🤝
**Engagement Model:**
Exclusive, long-term professional engagement

💰
**Remuneration:**
Fixed monthly remuneration, commensurate with experience and capabilities

🏛️
**Firm Location:**
Delhi, with regional litigation operations

🔹 1. EXPERIENCE & ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS

The ideal candidate must possess:

* A minimum of
  **5–6 years of post-qualification experience (PQE)**
  in core litigation practice.
* An LL.B. degree and a Master's degree in Law (LL.M.).
* Both LL.B. and LL.M. qualifications from
  **Tier-1 law institutions**
  .
* Substantial practical exposure to court proceedings, legal drafting, filing procedures, case management, and oral advocacy.
* The ability to independently manage matters, take ownership of assigned responsibilities, and provide sound legal advice based on facts, evidence, applicable law, and judicial precedents.

🔹 2. PRACTICE AREAS

The candidate should have practical experience and professional exposure across the following areas:

* **Civil Litigation**
* **Commercial Litigation**
* Business and Contractual Disputes
* Consumer Litigation
* Labour and Employment Matters
* Arbitration and Dispute Resolution
* Criminal Litigation

**The primary focus will be Civil and Commercial Litigation.**

Applicants should have demonstrable experience in handling civil and commercial disputes, including the preparation of pleadings, interim applications, replies, written submissions, evidence-related proceedings, and oral arguments.

🔹 3. INDEPENDENT CASE STRATEGY & COURTROOM ADVOCACY

We are looking for an advocate who can think independently, analyse disputes critically, and develop a litigation strategy rather than merely execute instructions.

The selected candidate should be capable of:

* Analysing facts, documents, evidence, and legal issues to identify the strengths and weaknesses of a case.
* Designing a practical, well-researched, and legally sustainable litigation strategy.
* Conducting in-depth legal research and identifying relevant judgments, statutory provisions, and judicial precedents.
* Drafting high-quality petitions, plaints, written statements, replies, applications, affidavits, written submissions, and other pleadings.
* Independently managing filing procedures, procedural requirements, and court deadlines.
* Preparing for hearings, anticipating opposing arguments, and presenting persuasive oral arguments.
* Identifying appropriate interim remedies, procedural options, settlement opportunities, and further legal steps.
* Evaluating litigation risks and advising on the most effective course of action to pursue the client's legitimate interests.

**The expectation is to engage a professional who can take ownership of a matter from its initial assessment through the appropriate stages of litigation.**

🔹 4. COURT ORDER COMPLIANCE & END-TO-END MATTER MANAGEMENT

The advocate must be capable of independently managing judicial directions, procedural timelines, and post-hearing requirements.

Responsibilities will include:

* Reviewing and analysing court orders immediately after hearings.
* Identifying directions requiring action, documentation, filing, or compliance.
* Monitoring deadlines and ensuring timely procedural steps.
* Preparing and coordinating compliance documents, applications, and subsequent filings.
* Tracking hearing dates, case progress, orders, and future action points.
* Keeping the firm's central team informed of developments, risks, compliance requirements, and recommended next steps.
* Ensuring that assigned matters are managed systematically and that avoidable procedural delays are minimised.

We value professionals who understand that effective litigation requires not only courtroom advocacy but also meticulous preparation, follow-through, and accountability.

🔹 5. EXCLUSIVE PROFESSIONAL ASSOCIATION & MONTHLY REMUNERATION

This opportunity is intended for an advocate seeking a structured, stable, and long-term professional association with a growing litigation law firm.

The selected candidate will be engaged on a
**monthly remuneration basis under mutually agreed exclusive engagement terms**
.

The professional will be expected to devote the agreed capacity to the firm's assigned matters and regional responsibilities, maintain appropriate coordination with the Delhi team, and ensure consistent handling of the firm's litigation work in the region.

We are particularly interested in candidates who value continuity of work, professional stability, long-term collaboration, and the opportunity to contribute to the development of a regional litigation practice.

The precise engagement terms, responsibilities, exclusivity arrangements, and remuneration will be mutually agreed upon, subject to applicable professional regulations.

🔹 6. REGIONAL REPRESENTATION & PRACTICE DEVELOPMENT

The selected advocate will serve as the firm's principal litigation professional for Bengaluru and the surrounding region within the agreed scope of engagement.

The responsibilities will include:

* Managing and representing the firm's assigned matters before appropriate courts and tribunals, subject to applicable enrolment, practice, and procedural requirements.
* Independently handling matters while coordinating with the firm's central team in Delhi.
* Maintaining regular communication with clients and relevant stakeholders in a professional and confidential manner.
* Coordinating with briefing counsel and other legal professionals whenever required.
* Preparing timely matter updates, hearing reports, case status summaries, and recommendations.
* Maintaining proper documentation and ensuring continuity in the management of each assigned matter.
* Helping establish and strengthen the firm's regional litigation operations through dependable execution and professional conduct.

We seek someone who can operate independently while remaining aligned with the firm's standards, systems, and client-service expectations.

🔹 7. LOCAL LANGUAGE & REGIONAL COURT FAMILIARITY

Familiarity with
**Kannada and English**
, local court procedures, regional litigation practices, and the ability to communicate effectively with clients and other stakeholders in Karnataka will be an added advantage.

An understanding of the local legal environment and practical experience appearing before courts and tribunals in the region will also be valuable.

🔹 8. THE PROFESSIONAL WE ARE LOOKING FOR

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

* Strong analytical and legal reasoning skills.
* Excellent legal research, drafting, and oral advocacy capabilities.
* Independent judgment and strategic thinking.
* A high degree of responsibility and professional integrity.
* Discipline in managing deadlines, court orders, and procedural compliance.
* Clear communication and effective coordination with a central legal team.
* The ability to manage assigned matters with minimal supervision.
* A collaborative approach to building a long-term professional association.

We are looking for someone who is serious about litigation, confident in their abilities, committed to high standards of legal work, and prepared to take meaningful responsibility for the matters entrusted to them.

🔹 HOW TO APPLY

Interested candidates are requested to share their updated résumé through either of the following channels:

📧
**Email:**
contact@jurisiti.com

📱
**WhatsApp:**
+91 97173 29850

Please mention
**“Core Litigation Advocate – Bengaluru”**
in the email subject line or WhatsApp message.

Candidates are encouraged to include a brief overview of their post-qualification experience, educational qualifications, principal practice areas, courts and tribunals regularly appeared before, and representative litigation experience, subject to client confidentiality.

**We look forward to connecting with a capable litigation advocate who can take ownership of assigned matters, represent the firm professionally, and help build a strong regional litigation practice in Bengaluru.**

**Build. Represent. Strategise. Litigate. Grow.**

* #Hiring #LegalJobs #AdvocateJobs #BengaluruJobs #BangaloreLawyers #LitigationAdvocate #CivilLitigation #CommercialLitigation #LegalCareers #LawFirm #Arbitration #DisputeResolution #LegalProfession

title: Employee Relations Business Partner, India (Contractor)
description:
**About Rippling**
Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.
  
  
Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.
  
  
Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.
  
  
We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.
  
  
**About The Role**
Rippling is looking for an Employee Relations Business Partner based in Bangalore, India to join its HR Policy & Compliance Team to manage employee relations investigations.
  
  
You will work closely with a number of stakeholders, including HR Business Partners (HRBPs), Legal, and business leaders, on employee relations investigations.
  
  
**What You Will Do**

* Assess incoming employee relations concerns, determine the appropriate investigative response, and partner with stakeholders to drive timely and thoughtful resolution.
* Partner closely with Legal to identify and escalate matters requiring a dedicated Legal team investigation.
* Work with HR Business Partners, managers, and business leaders to resolve employee relations matters in a way that is fair, consistent, risk-aware, and operationally practical.
* Provide practical HR guidance and recommendations that address employee concerns while supporting team effectiveness, manager accountability, and business continuity.
* Draft clear, concise documentation, including case summaries, findings, recommendations, stakeholder updates, playbooks, templates, and business-facing guidance.
* Track employee relations activity, themes, resolution status, and outcomes in Rippling.
* Identify patterns, root causes, and emerging risks across employee relations matters, and recommend process, training, manager coaching, or policy improvements.
* Help develop and maintain employee relations operating practices, including intake criteria, escalation guidelines, documentation standards, investigation protocols, templates, and cadences.
* Leverage data, AI, and automation to improve employee relations processes, scale case handling, and create better experiences for employees and managers.
* Maintain discretion, confidentiality, neutrality, and professionalism when handling sensitive employee and workplace matters.

**What You Will Need**

* 5+ years of experience in employee relations, HR business partnership, HR compliance, workplace investigations, or a related HR role.
* Strong understanding of employee relations principles, workplace conduct standards, HR compliance considerations, and investigation best practices.
* Experience advising managers and business leaders on sensitive employee matters with sound judgment, discretion, neutrality, and empathy.
* Ability to assess employee relations concerns and determine the right path for HR-led resolution, stakeholder partnership, or escalation to Legal, Compliance, Security, or another specialized team.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience drafting case summaries, findings, recommendations, playbooks, and stakeholder updates.
* Strong interviewing, fact-gathering, documentation, problem-solving, and analytical skills.
* Practical business judgment and strong HR instincts, with the ability to recommend solutions that are fair, consistent, risk-aware, and operationally realistic.
* Strong project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple matters at once, prioritize urgent issues, and drive work to timely resolution.
* Experience working cross-functionally with HRBPs, Legal, managers, executives, and other internal stakeholders.
* Ability to use data and case trends to identify recurring issues, improve processes, and support broader employee relations priorities.
* Comfort building structure, improving processes, and operating effectively in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.
* Interest in using AI and automation to scale HR processes and improve the employee and manager experience.

****Nice to have****

* Law degree, such as a JD or equivalent.
* Experience with Jira, case-management systems, HRIS tools, or similar tracking platforms.
* Experience supporting a global or multi-state workforce.
* Experience building employee relations programs, operating models, templates, or playbooks in a scaling company.

title: Associate Partner / Principal Associate - Corporate Advisory
description:
Role: Associate Partner / Principal Associate - Corporate Advisory

Location: Bengaluru

**About Aarna Law:**

Aarna Law is a counsel-led dispute resolution and litigation boutique with offices in Bengaluru, Delhi, and Mumbai. Founded by Shreyas Jayasimha and Kamala Nagganand, the firm advises Indian and international clients across arbitration, commercial litigation, corporate advisory, and private client practice, and has had the privilege of representing the Republic of India.

The practice draws on a legacy of over a century of legal service, having advised more than 1,500 clients and resolved disputes exceeding six billion dollars in value. It is built around a simple idea: understand the client deeply, and bring rigour, integrity, and good judgment to every matter. We take our work seriously, and each other less so.

**Job description:**

We are looking for a dynamic and commercially astute a Associate Partner / Principal Associate to join the Corporate Advisory practice. The role offers an opportunity to advise domestic and international clients on a broad spectrum of corporate and commercial matters, including corporate restructuring, and general corporate advisory. The ideal candidate should possess strong drafting, negotiation, analytical, and client management skills, with the ability to independently handle transactions while mentoring junior team members.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Advise clients on corporate and commercial laws, regulatory matters, and governance issues.
* Draft, review, and negotiate a wide range of transaction and commercial documents, including:
* Share Purchase Agreements (SPA), Shareholders' Agreements (SHA), Subscription Agreements (SSA), Joint Venture Agreements (JVA), Business Transfer Agreements (BTA), Asset Purchase Agreements, Commercial contracts and service agreements, Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDA)
* Term Sheets and Memoranda of Understanding (MoU)
* Conduct legal due diligence and prepare due diligence reports.
* Advise on company law, corporate governance, foreign investment, and regulatory compliance.
* Liaise with clients, regulators, consultants, and opposing counsel throughout transactions.
* Identify legal risks and provide practical, business-oriented solutions.
* Manage multiple transactions and ensure timely delivery of assignments.
* Supervise, mentor, and review the work of junior associates.
* Contribute to business development initiatives, client pitches, articles, knowledge sessions, and practice development activities.

Qualifications

* LL.B. from a recognised university.
* LL.M will be an added advantage.

Experience

* min 8+ years of post-qualification experience in a reputed law firm.
* Significant experience in Corporate Advisory and General Corporate Advisory.
* Managed a team of Corporate Lawyers

Desired Skills

* Strong understanding of the Companies Act, 2013 and related corporate laws.
* Knowledge of FEMA, FDI regulations, SEBI regulations (where applicable), and other regulatory frameworks.
* Excellent drafting, negotiation, and legal research skills.
* Strong commercial acumen with the ability to provide practical legal advice.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Ability to independently manage complex transactions and client relationships.
* Strong organisational and project management skills.
* Team-oriented with mentoring and leadership capabilities.

**Job Description**
**Specialist — Commercial Standards, Claims & Contracts is a Business Analyst and SME on the Customer Operations Transformation programme.**
The outcome is a clear, governed set of commercial policies — credit, claims, pricing and trade terms — and customer agreements that are standard, compliant and correctly executed in the systems; fewer and cleaner customer claims; lower invalid deductions and trade-spend leakage; and <1 Day Resolution wherever the process allows: fewer claims arising in the first place, and faster, controlled settlement for those that remain. Everything this role does serves that outcome.
  
  
The scope spans Commercial Standards, Claims and Contracts end to end — formulation and governance of credit, claims, pricing and trade-terms policies, policy exceptions and delegation of authority, the customer agreement and contract lifecycle (drafting, approval, activation, amendment and renewal), pricing, rebate, discount and promotion setup, accruals, claims intake, validation and settlement, proof of performance, and the controls that link agreed terms to what is invoiced and paid. The role designs across this scope as one process rather than as separate contract, promotion and claims solutions. It works with market Commercial, Revenue Growth Management, Sales Finance, Credit, Legal, Internal Control, Customer Service and Collections teams, GBO, D&T, the SAP and Control Tower (Claims and Deduction platform) teams and third-party vendors.
  
  
The role combines 5 capabilities in one person. As an SME, they formulate, document the global commercial policies — credit policy (credit limits, payment terms, risk categories, blocks and releases), claims policy (eligibility, evidence, time limits, approval and write-off thresholds), and pricing governance (price-setting and approval, discount and rebate guardrails, price-change control) — and the standards and controls that make them work in practice. As a business analyst, they interrogate contract, trade-terms, accrual, claims and deduction data, document current and target process, and write requirements to standard. As a subject matter expert, they bring the functional depth to act as design authority for the fragment and to challenge solutions that would not work in the markets. As a sprint or project owner, they take a scope fragment through design, test and deployment on a two to four week value drop cadence. As a process and technology expert, they translate commercial policy, contract terms and controls into working design on SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, Control Tower claims and deduction capability, and the contract and trade promotion management toolset.
  
  
**The defining discipline of this role is designing claims out at source, not processing them faster.**
A quicker claim approval is a smaller prize than a contract term clear enough never to be disputed; a faster settlement is a smaller prize than a promotion set up correctly in the system so the customer never needs to claim. The postholder is expected to use the data to find where in the commercial process claims are created — an ambiguous contract clause, a non-standard trade term, a late or incorrect pricing or promotion setup, an accrual gap, a weak approval control — and design the fix upstream into commercial policy, standards, contract templates, deal approval and master data, as well as into the claims and settlement design.
  
  
**Understanding of markets and of upstream and downstream impact is central to the role.**
A claim usually starts life as a commercial negotiation; a contract term becomes a pricing condition, an accrual, an invoice and, if anything is misaligned, a deduction in Collections. The postholder is expected to know what happens on either side of their own process — from deal negotiation through to cash and the P&L — and to design accordingly.
  
  
**This is a transformation design and delivery role, not an operational one.**
The postholder does not negotiate customer deals, draft or approve individual contracts, validate or settle individual claims, or manage customer relationships; that stays with market Commercial, Legal, GBO and BPO run teams. The role changes how that work is done — including the commercial policies, standards, contract templates, reason codes, analytics and controls that let run teams find and remove causes in BAU. The role formulates and recommends policy; final approval sits with the relevant policy owners and governance forums.
  
  
The role works independently within an agreed frame set by the workstream lead, gathers its own data, forms its own view and brings recommendations rather than questions. Where a Senior Specialist is assigned on the same fragment, it works under their design direction. Decisions are expected to be based on evidence rather than opinion, and every artefact is expected to meet the programme documentation, taxonomy and quality standards, including BPQMS.
  
  
**Analyse commercial terms, contracts and claims performance and baseline the problem — 25%.**
Document current-state credit, claims and pricing policies, commercial standards, contract lifecycle and claims processes across markets and identify variation from the global standard. Build the process, trade-terms and claim-type taxonomy and interrogate the data directly at portfolio level — customer agreements and terms, pricing and promotion conditions, accruals versus actuals, claims volume, value, ageing and rejection rates, invalid deductions, write-offs and trade-spend leakage — to baseline the problem per market and size the opportunity. Perform gap analysis between current process, commercial policy, contract terms, platform capability, controls and the target operating model, separating structural design issues from operational backlog. Support business-rule validation, master-data requirements and policy analysis. Aim for validated current-state documentation and a defensible baseline that will stand up to audit.
  
  
**Formulate commercial policies and standards, and design claims out at source — 25%.**
Support future-state design aligned to the global standard, always designing for the cause rather than the symptom. Formulate, document and maintain the global commercial policies the design depends on — credit policy (credit limits and risk categorisation, payment terms, credit blocks and release authority), claims policy (claim eligibility, evidence and proof-of-performance requirements, submission time limits, validation, approval and write-off thresholds) and pricing governance (price-setting and approval, discount, rebate and promotion guardrails, price-change control and margin protection) — with a clear policy-exception and delegation-of-authority framework, and take them through the governance forums for approval. Translate policy into the standards that operationalise it: standard trade-terms structures, contract and agreement templates, clause libraries, deal approval and delegation-of-authority rules, and the minimum data a contract must carry to be executed correctly in the systems. Use the baseline to show where claims are created — contract ambiguity, non-standard terms, pricing and promotion setup, accruals, proof of performance, master data — and design the fix upstream. Design the interventions: standard contract-to-condition setup, automated accruals and settlement, validated claim intake, reason-code frameworks and claims workflow. Prepare business requirements, functional specifications, process flows, business rules and user stories. Facilitate design workshops and document outcomes and decisions. Assess process, policy, financial and control impacts, and define how policy compliance will be monitored.
  
  
Deliver the outcome: standard contracts, fewer claims and <1 Day Resolution — 20%. Design for, and evidence, policy adoption and compliance across markets, an increase in contracts on standard terms and templates, fewer policy exceptions, a reduction in claims volume, aged claims, invalid deductions and trade-spend leakage, and movement toward <1 Day Resolution for appropriate claims and queries. Shape the build-out of SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, Control Tower claims and deduction functionality, and contract and trade promotion management tooling as the primary levers on the outcome. Define the measures with the business owner, monitor post-go-live performance against the baseline, and recommend and, where owned, implement continuous improvements to the design. This is the accountability every other accountability serves.
  
  
**Own testing, deployment and adoption through the value drops — 20%.**
Translate requirements into working design on SAP, Control Tower and the contract and trade promotion management toolset with D&T, system integrators and vendors. Define and review test scenarios, support SIT and UAT, and manage defect resolution with business users. Break the work into fragments that can be delivered on the value drop cadence, and own the backlog, dependencies and risks for the fragment. Support deployment, hypercare and business readiness, and hand over up-to-date commercial standards, contract templates, process documentation, SOPs, controls and training materials to the run teams. Aim for SIT and UAT completed with minimal post-go-live defects and a clean handover into run.
  
  
**Manage delivery discipline and enable across the programme — 10%.**
Track requirements, risks, assumptions, dependencies and decisions throughout the lifecycle, and escalate early and precisely when the frame is wrong. Act as a trusted partner to market Commercial, Revenue Growth Management, Sales Finance, Credit, Legal, Internal Control, Customer Service, GBO, D&T and vendors, and coach business users through testing, deployment and adoption. Enable the adjacent workstreams — Order-to-Invoice, Collections, Claims & Receivables, Customer Service and Supply — by surfacing cross-boundary impact before it becomes a deployment defect, and by handing design-level root causes to the workstream that owns them.
  
  

* Commercial Standards, Claims & Contracts domain depth and business analysis, on a broad Customer Operations base. Real SME depth in commercial policy and customer contracts — credit policy and credit risk, claims policy, pricing governance, trade-terms structures, rebates, discounts and promotions, contract lifecycle management, accruals, and claims validation and settlement — sufficient to act as design authority and to write policy that is clear, enforceable and auditable, combined with strong business-analysis craft: process mapping, requirements gathering, gap analysis, functional-specification writing, user stories and workshop facilitation. Understands how claims and deductions are created across the commercial and Order to Cash process, and how contract wording, deal approval, pricing and promotion setup, master data and accruals drive them. Built on a general understanding of Customer Operations end-to-end (Order to Cash, Commercial and Supply) and of how markets actually work, including upstream and downstream impact. Knows Consumer Products industry standards and the realities of Beer, Wine & Spirits — distributor and wholesaler concentration, complex customer agreements, promotional and trade-spend claims, and route-to-market and regulatory constraints on trade terms. Working knowledge of Diageo BPQMS standards.
* Data, technology and delivery discipline. Comfortable interrogating contract, trade-terms, accrual, claims and deduction data directly, and translating requirements into working design on SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, the Control Tower claims and deduction platform, and the supporting contract and trade promotion management toolset. Understands the platform, the data model, the business rules, workflow and approval logic, and the operating model — retained, GBO and BPO — beneath the process. Strong on test planning and defect management (SIT / UAT), business readiness and hypercare, and on risk, issue and dependency management. Data-driven by instinct — baselines the problem, quantifies the opportunity and lets the evidence settle the argument. Able to prioritise across concurrent workstreams and deadlines.
* Design-for-prevention rigour, stakeholder influence and adaptability. Relentless about cause over symptom in design — not satisfied with automating a workaround when the claim could be designed out through a clearer standard, contract or setup. Strong stakeholder management and influencing across a global and local matrix, including senior Commercial, Finance and Legal stakeholders and policy governance forums, and consultative by default: frames the problem before prescribing and drives stakeholders toward aligned design decisions. Clear communicator, and able to manage conflict to a resolution rather than let it stall a decision. Comfortable being redeployed: arrives in an unfamiliar market or process, orients fast, and adds value quickly. Resilient, collaborative, and a visible role model for Diageo’s values.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience in Finance, Business, Commercial, Law, Operations, IT or a related discipline.
* Working knowledge of Diageo BPQMS standards. Business-analysis, Agile / Scrum or Lean Six Sigma credentials are an advantage; familiarity with SAP pricing, condition contracts or settlement management, Control Tower or similar claims and deduction platforms, or contract lifecycle or trade promotion management tools is a plus.

**Experience — Essential**

* Overall. 10+ years spanning transformation, business analysis and consultative experience, with a strong core of business analysis and SME design work in large-scale process transformation.
* Subject matter expertise. Deep functional understanding of credit, claims and pricing policy, commercial terms, customer contracts and agreements, trade promotions and claims within a Commercial and Order-to-Cash environment — someone who knows how claims and deductions are created by contract terms and commercial setup, and how standards and process should be designed to prevent them, not only the tooling. Operational exposure is useful context; the requirement is designing the process, not running it.
* Transformation. Experience in business process transformation, including current-state assessment and future-state operating model design, across the full lifecycle from design through testing, deployment and post-go-live stabilisation. Evidence of reducing claims, deductions, trade-spend leakage, cycle time or manual effort against a defensible baseline.
* Consultative. A track record of acting as a trusted business partner — framing the real problem, facilitating design decisions, aligning global and local stakeholders — and being measured on whether the business changed, not only on whether the deliverable shipped.
* Technology. Experience translating business requirements into functional specifications and solution design with D&T, system integrators and vendors, including test planning and defect management (SIT / UAT). SAP pricing, condition contracts or settlement management, Control Tower, or comparable contract, trade promotion or claims platform exposure is an advantage.
* Industry. FMCG or Consumer Products experience is essential. Beer, Wine & Spirits experience is strongly preferred.
* General understanding of Customer Operations end to end — OTC, Commercial and Supply — and of how markets actually operate, including upstream and downstream impact.

**Experience — Desirable**

* Experience formulating and governing commercial policy — credit, claims and pricing governance — and the standards beneath it: trade-terms frameworks, contract templates, clause libraries and deal approval policies — across multiple markets.
* Exposure to contract lifecycle management, trade promotion management, or claims and settlement automation, including AI-led claim validation and matching.
* Experience designing reason-code frameworks and claims analytics that let run teams identify and remove the causes of claims and deductions.
* Experience defining what must be global standard versus what requires market localisation.
* Experience working in a pooled, on-demand or competency-based delivery model across multiple workstreams.
* Prior experience of a GBO or shared services transition or operating model consolidation.

**About Us**
With over 200 brands sold in nearly 180 countries, Diageo is home to some of the world’s most iconic drinks. From Johnnie Walker and Guinness to Tanqueray, Smirnoff and Don Julio, we craft brands chosen for life’s moments — from everyday connections to landmark celebrations.

**Company Description**
Version 1 has celebrated 30 years in business and continues to be trusted by global brands to deliver technology and transformation solutions that drive customer success. Our deep expertise enables our customers to navigate the rapidly evolving technology landscape. We foster strong partnerships with global technology leaders including Microsoft, AWS, Oracle, Red Hat, OutSystems, Snowflake, ensuring that our customers are provided with the highest quality solutions and services.
  
  
We’re an award-winning employer reflecting how our employees are at the very heart of  what we do:
  
  

* UK & Ireland's premier AWS, Microsoft & Oracle partner
* 3300+ strong, €350/£300m revenue business
* 10+ years as a Great Place to Work in Ireland & UK
* Best Workplace for Women in the UK & Ireland by GPTW
* Best Workplace for Wellbeing in the UK by GPTW

We’re a core values driven company, we hire people who share our values, and we reward those who display and foster them, it’s deeply embedded within our DNA. Invest in us and we’ll invest in you!.
  
  
**Job Description**
**Purpose**
Own the post-signature contract lifecycle for Version 1, taking ownership of every executed contract from signature onwards. You will make sure contract data is accurate, obligations are tracked, contracted price uplifts are applied on time, and renewals are never missed, so the business has reliable backlog revenue visibility and strong compliance evidence.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Own the post-signature contract management process, governance model and all escalations.
* Run the price uplift and indexation cycle, and hold approval sign-off before increases are applied.
* Sign off renewal actions and own the working relationship with sales and finance.
* Maintain the accuracy and completeness of contract data against an agreed standard.
* Oversee the renewal early-warning routine so renewals are actioned well ahead of expiry.
* Produce and own backlog revenue and compliance reporting.
* Set and maintain service levels for contract intake, data validation and renewal alerts.
* Drive automation and AI adoption so the function scales without adding headcount.

**What Makes This Role Distinctive**

* High volume: the function handles 150 to 200 signed contracts every month.
* Lean by design: a small, focused team where automation and AI carry the routine work and the team manages exceptions rather than processing every record by hand.
* You will work with the company contract lifecycle management platform and CRM. Full training is provided; prior experience with these specific systems is not required.

**Qualifications**
**Required skills and experience**

* Substantial experience in contract management, covering the post-signature lifecycle: obligations, renewals, and price or indexation clauses.
* A strong governance mindset, comfortable owning process, approvals and escalations.
* Commercial acumen: understands backlog revenue, gross profit, and how contracts translate into reported revenue.
* Confident stakeholder management across sales and finance.
* High attention to detail and a firm grip on data accuracy.
* Comfortable working in a lean, automation-first way, focusing effort on exceptions and outliers.
* Around 8 to 14 years of experience in contract management, including time at a lead or senior level.

**Desirable**

* Exposure to any contract lifecycle management (CLM) tooling.
* Experience in a managed services, IT services or technology environment.
* Experience introducing automation or AI into a contract or commercial operations process.

**Additional Information**
Why Version 1?
  
  
At Version 1, we believe in providing our employees with a comprehensive benefits package that prioritises their wellbeing, professional growth, and financial stability.
  
  

* Share in our success with our Quarterly Performance-Related Profit Share Scheme, where employees collectively benefit from a share of our company's profits
* Strong Career Progression & mentorship coaching through our Strength in Balance & Leadership schemes with a dedicated quarterly Pathways Career Development programme
* Flexible/remote working, Version 1 is tremendously understanding of life events and people’s individual circumstances and offer flexibility to help achieve a healthy work life balance
* Financial Wellbeing initiatives including; Pension, Private Healthcare Cover, Life Assurance, Financial advice and an Employee Discount scheme
* Employee Wellbeing schemes including Gym Discounts, Bike to Work, Fitness classes, Mindfulness Workshops, Employee Assistance Programme and much more. Generous holiday allowance, enhanced maternity/paternity leave, marriage/civil partnership leave and special leave policies
* Educational assistance, incentivised certifications, and accreditations, including AWS, Microsoft, Oracle, and Red Hat
* Reward schemes including Version 1’s Annual Excellence Awards & ‘Call-Out’ platform.
* Environment, Social and Community First initiatives allow you to get involved in local fundraising and development opportunities as part of fostering our diversity, inclusion and belonging schemes.

And many more exciting benefits… drop us a note to find out more.
  
  
Version 1 is an equal opportunities employer.
  
  
We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone feels valued and able to thrive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and lived experiences, and we value the different perspectives people bring including those shaped by disability and neurodiversity.
  
  
We want every candidate to have a positive and accessible recruitment experience. If you need reasonable adjustments at any stage of the process, please contact your recruiter at Version 1. We will consider all requests carefully, respectfully and confidentially.

The company delivers comprehensive systems, including foam, hydrant, sprinkler, spray, extinguishers, fire alarm systems, and gas suppression solutions for high‑hazard industries and government projects. A dedicated AMC division ensures ongoing maintenance, manned support, and system readiness in case of fire incidents. The Articleship Company Secretary role is a full-time, on-site position based in Bengaluru. The Articleship trainee will help in coordinating with internal departments and external stakeholders, compiling data and reports for compliance and audits, and maintaining accurate records for secretarial practices. * Should demonstrate proficiency in MS Office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and basic digital record management for maintaining secretarial and compliance data.
* Should possess effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to coordinate with cross-functional teams and external professionals in a professional manner.
* Should demonstrate strong analytical, organizational, and time management abilities, along with a proactive and ethical approach to confidentiality and data integrity.

title: Site Contracts Negotiator II
description:
Site Contracts Negotiator with experience in ANZ region - India
  
  
ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.
  
  
As a values-driven organisation, integrity, collaboration, agility, and inclusion are at the heart of how we work and interact with each other, customers, patients and suppliers.
  
  
As a Site Contracts Negotiator at ICON, you will independently manage the negotiation and execution of clinical trial agreements and budgets for a range of studies. You will work closely with sites and internal stakeholders to support efficient and compliant study start-up.
  
  
**What You Will Do**
You will contribute to contract management activities, taking responsibility for your deliverables and working collaboratively.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities Include**

* Negotiating site contracts and budgets with investigator sites, within defined parameters and playbooks.
* Reviewing and adapting contract language to reflect sponsor requirements, local laws, and site feedback.
* Managing a portfolio of contracts, monitoring cycle times, and proactively addressing barriers to execution.
* Collaborating with legal, finance, and project teams to resolve contractual questions and ensure alignment.
* Maintaining accurate records of negotiations, approvals, and executed agreements in relevant systems.
* Supporting continuous improvement in contract templates, processes, and guidance, and mentoring junior colleagues where appropriate.

**Your Profile**
You will bring relevant contract management experience, along with the following qualifications and skills.
  
  
**Required Qualifications And Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in law, business, life sciences, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* 4+ years of experience in site contracting, negotiating and managing clinical trial agreements within CRO, pharma, or healthcare.
* Experience working for Australia and New Zealand
* Shift Working - 6 AM to 2 PM IST
* Good understanding of clinical trial agreements and budget negotiation principles.
* Strong negotiation, communication, and organisational skills.
* Ability to manage multiple contracts and timelines, with attention to detail and quality.

title: Commercial Compliance Manager, APAC
description:
**Bring more to life.**
Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference within life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology?
  
  
At Cytiva, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact.
  
  
You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.
  
  
Working at Cytiva means being at the forefront of providing new solutions to transform human health. Our incredible customers undertake life saving activities ranging from fundamental biological research to developing innovative vaccines, new medicines, and cell and gene therapies.
  
  
At Cytiva you will be able to continuously improve yourself and us – working on challenges that truly matter with people that care for each other, our customers, and their patients. Take your next step to an altogether life-changing career.
  
  
Learn about the Danaher Business System which makes everything possible.
  
  
The
**Commercial Compliance Manager**
plays a pivotal role in protecting Cytiva's reputation and enabling sustainable growth by bringing our Commercial Compliance Program to life. Working closely with business and functional leaders, you will translate compliance expectations into practical, risk-based solutions, strengthen ethical decision-making, and use data, technology and AI to identify emerging risks and drive measurable improvement across our global commercial activities.
  
  
This position reports to the Senior Director, Compliance, Commercial and Operations and is part of the Legal and Compliance function. The role will be based on-site in Bangalore, India.
  
  
**What You Will Do**

* Channel Partner Compliance Management: Lead the effective implementation of policies and controls for third-party distributors. Partner with business leaders to assess, manage and monitor Channel Partner risk, resolve red flags, and ensure due diligence and approvals are completed in line with company requirements.
* Customer Interactions: Enable compliant and effective customer engagement by implementing relevant policies, advising stakeholders on higher-risk activities, supporting risk-based approvals, and meeting applicable local transparency reporting obligations.
* Auditing and Monitoring: Deliver risk-based auditing and monitoring activities, apply sound judgement and data-led analysis to selected transactions, identify root causes and emerging trends, and recommend proportionate corrective and preventive actions.
* Training and Communications: Create and deliver engaging, practical compliance training and communications for employees and third parties, including train-the-trainer sessions where appropriate, and assess whether learning is translating into changed behaviour.
* Systems, Data and AI Enablement: Support and continuously improve global Legal and Compliance systems, including user support, training and system maintenance. Use analytics, automation and approved AI tools to monitor adoption, identify potential non-compliance, improve workflow efficiency and generate actionable insights, while maintaining appropriate human oversight and protecting confidential information.

**Who You Are**

* BA/BS degree, or global equivalent, in Law, Finance, Information Technology, Business or a related discipline.
* Substantial experience designing, implementing or managing compliance, legal, regulatory, audit or risk programs, preferably in healthcare, life sciences or another regulated industry.
* Outstanding written and verbal communication skills in English, with the confidence to influence stakeholders across cultures, functions and levels of seniority.
* Strong data and analytical capability, including building reliable data collection methods, using quantitative and qualitative analysis to assess compliance performance, identifying trends and translating insights into management action.
* Demonstrated ability to use AI and digital tools as part of daily work to improve the quality, speed and consistency of research, analysis, monitoring, communication and process execution, while applying appropriate judgement, validation and data protection controls. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and the wider Microsoft 365 suite is also required.

**It Would Be a Plus If You Also Possess**

* Experience managing compliance programs in a regulated environment, including oversight of third-party distributors or other Channel Partners.
* Professional proficiency in an additional language relevant to the region, particularly Japanese or Korean.

Cytiva, a Danaher operating company, offers a broad array of comprehensive, competitive benefit programs that add value to our lives. Whether it’s a health care program or paid time off, our programs contribute to life beyond the job. Check out our benefits at Danaher Benefits Info.
  
  
Join our winning team today. Together, we’ll accelerate the real-life impact of tomorrow’s science and technology. We partner with customers across the globe to help them solve their most complex challenges, architecting solutions that bring the power of science to life.
  
  
For more information, visit www.danaher.com.

title: Company Secretary
description:
At Ball, integrity and trust are the foundation of who we are. Guided by our core values—"We Care. We Work. We Win.”—we create a culture where every voice matters and every idea drives progress.
  
  
Further your career at Ball, a world leader in manufacturing sustainable aluminium packaging. Achieve extraordinary things when you join our team, and make a difference in your professional development, the community, and around the globe!
  
  
Create a new future. Apply Today.
  
  
**Position Overview**
The Company Secretary (CS) is responsible for ensuring full compliance with statutory, legal, and regulatory requirements applicable to the organization. The role ensures effective corporate governance, supports the Board of Directors, manages secretarial records, ensures timely filings under the Companies Act, 2013 and related laws, and support corporate decision making.
  
  
The Company Secretary acts as a key link between the Board, senior management, regulators, auditors, and stakeholders. The role also oversees legal compliance, contract management, risk mitigation, and supports corporate initiatives such as mergers, expansions, and statutory audits.
  
  
Ensures that the company operates with the highest standards of governance, transparency, and ethical practices.
  
  
**Your Key Responsibilities Include**
**Corporate Governance & Board Management**

* Organize and document Board, Committee, and General Meetings as per Companies Act, 2013.
* Prepare agendas, notices, resolutions, and supporting papers.
* Maintain statutory registers and minutes (physical/electronic).
* Advise Board on governance, compliance, corporate responsibilities & secretarial practices.
* File statutory returns (AOC‑4, MGT‑7, DIR‑3 KYC, MSME, etc.) on time.

**Statutory & Regulatory Compliance**

* Ensure compliance with Companies Act, FEMA regulations, SEBI regulations (if applicable) etc
* Liaise with ROC, MCA, RBI, SEBI, and other regulators.
* Track legal changes and guide management on required actions.
* Manage CSR compliance, documentation, and committee support.

**Legal & Contract Management ( If Required )**

* Draft, review, and vet contracts, vendor agreements, NDAs, and service/purchase agreements.
* Maintain contract repository and manage renewals.
* Support legal matters, disputes, arbitration, in consultation with the Legal team.

**Secretarial & Documentation Control**

* Maintain statutory registers (Members, Directors, Charges, Contracts, etc.).
* Manage share certificates, transfers, and related records.
* Handle loan/charge documentation and coordinate with banks.

**Risk Management & Internal Controls**

* Identify compliance risks and implement mitigation measures.
* Support internal, statutory, and secretarial audits.
* Develop compliance checklists, SOPs, and internal control systems.
* Based on the company’s framework of Compliance Calendar - follow-up with respective teams for the confirmation of compliance of the Applicable Laws.
* Managing the Internal Compliance tool of the Company & preparing the monthly compliance chart.
* Providing the Financial Impact assessment of Non-Compliance of other corporate Laws to the Board.
* Review of Organization Approval Matrix and assessing the implementation of the Matrix and its functionality.

**Stakeholder Management**

* Act as primary contact for shareholders, regulators, auditors, and authorities.
* Support investor relations (if applicable).
* Coordinate with Finance, HR, Operations, EHS, and Procurement Teams for organization-wide compliance.

**Corporate Strategy & Special Projects**

* Support M&A, JV, restructuring, and strategic initiatives.
* Draft policies, charters, and governance frameworks, in co-ordination with the Legal Team.
* Assist with expansion projects, plant registrations, and regulatory approvals.

**Other Responsibilities**

* Support insurance renewals and claims.
* Maintain confidentiality and be available during audits, inspections, and urgent compliance matters.

**What are we looking for?**

* Qualified Company Secretary (ACS / FCS) from ICSI.
* Law Degree (LLB).
* 6- 8 years of experience in secretarial and legal compliance roles in a manufacturing / engineering / industrial organization.
* Experience in handling Board meetings, statutory filings, and corporate governance.
* Exposure to contract management, legal documentation, and regulatory interactions.
* Experience in managing compliance for multi‑plant operations preferred.
* Strong knowledge of Companies Act, 2013, FEMA regulations, Labour Laws, and industrial regulations, and all applicable Corporate Laws.
* Legal and regulatory compliance expertise.
* Excellent drafting, documentation, and communication skills.
* High integrity, confidentiality, and ethical judgment.
* Ability to manage multiple stakeholders and deadlines, and advice on corporate restructuring & governance.
* Proficiency in MCA portal, e‑filings, and MS Office.
* Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills.
* English (Proficient).
* Local language (preferred).

Ball Corporation is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We actively encourage applications from everybody, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, faith, ability, or orientation. Our products range from infinitely recyclable aluminium cans, cups to aerosol bottles solutions that enable our customers to contribute to a better world.
  
  
Each of us has a deep commitment to diversity and inclusion which is the foundation of our culture of belonging. Everyone at Ball is making a difference by doing what we love. Because what we create may change, but what we will always make is a difference.
  
  
Please note the advertised job title might vary from the job title on the contract due to local job title structure and global HR systems.
  
  
Job Grade: Global Grade 10

title: Senior Executive, Technology Risk & Compliance
description:
PhonePe Limited (Formerly PhonePe Private Limited) is a technology company that builds digital platforms for Payments, Digital Distribution Services and Financial Services. Headquartered in India, the PhonePe digital payments app was launched in 2016. As of April 2026, PhonePe has over 70 Crore life-till-date registered users and a digital payments acceptance network spread across over 5 Crore merchants. PhonePe’s products and services include Consumer Payments (including Digital Distribution Services), Merchant Payments, Lending and Insurance Distribution services, and New Platforms, which comprise Share.Market (stock broking and mutual funds distribution platform), and Indus Appstore (Android-based mobile app marketplace). Culture:
  
  
At PhonePe, we go the extra mile to make sure you can bring your best self to work, Everyday!. And that starts with creating the right environment for you. We empower people and trust them to do the right thing. Here, you own your work from start to finish, right from day one. PhonePe-rs solve complex problems and execute quickly; often building frameworks from scratch. If you’re excited by the idea of building platforms that touch millions, ideating with some of the best minds in the country and executing on your dreams with purpose and speed, join us!
  
  
**Job Description**

* Contribute and point-out risks of the product/service during pre-planning work.
* Prepare the control checklist required for the review for each regulatory and unregulated functions
* Designing work programs and executing steps, meeting deadlines to evaluate compliance with rules and regulations.
* Interacting with senior heads of business and compliance as part of scoping, control design assessment, reporting findings and offering solutions to address control gaps or enhance processes.
* Formulate questions to be asked during walkthroughs and lead walkthroughs when called upon
* Identify controls after attending a walkthrough, specifically those related to the risks noted
* Provide rough drafts of issue documentation, identifying the important parts required.
* Define testing scripts, coordinate with respective development teams to run the same during the review process and evaluate the outcome along with the manager.
* Good eye for detailing with respect to each product regulations and controls

**Qualifications**

* Compliance Assurance (preferably also from a financial service e.g., banks, NBFC, Insurance firms, Stock Broking firms, Fintech etc) or is a former financial services industry employee that has led audits/ examinations/ compliance reviews /quality assessments /quality tests where the focus was Controls Testing (which very importantly includes (i) assessing the design of controls, and (ii) whether the controls are operating effectively) would be a good candidate. They would be the key & critical foundation. Basic AML/ OFAC experience would be preferred.
* At least 6 years of audit, compliance testing or monitoring, or relevant Compliance experience.
* Passion for technical compliance and be interested in conducting wide-scale investigative reviews.
* Have a good appreciation of the regulations applicable in India and APAC.
* Highly detail-oriented, motivated, curious individual with good time-management skills, analytical and communication skills
* Quick and sharp individual who relishes the challenges of understanding and interpreting regulations and processes across different businesses and jurisdictions.
* Strong communication, interpersonal and influencing skills. The candidate should have the ability to establish credibility and strong partnerships with senior business leaders, control functions and corporate partners globally.
* Fluency in written and spoken English is a must have. Excellent written skills, and ability to prepare clear, concise reports with minimal supervision.
* Have an audit and / or relevant industry qualifications, or a university degree.
* Proficiency in Excel and SQL is a preferred skill to have.

**Additional Information**
PhonePe Full Time Employee Benefits (Not applicable for Intern or Contract Roles)
  
  
Insurance Benefits - Medical Insurance, Critical Illness Insurance, Accidental Insurance, Life Insurance Wellness Program - Employee Assistance Program, Onsite Medical Center, Emergency Support System Parental Support - Maternity Benefit, Paternity Benefit Program, Adoption Assistance Program, Day-care Support Program Mobility Benefits - Relocation benefits, Transfer Support Policy, Travel Policy Retirement Benefits - Employee PF Contribution, Flexible PF Contribution, Gratuity, NPS, Leave Encashment Other Benefits - Higher Education Assistance, Car Lease, Salary Advance Policy
  
  
Our inclusive culture promotes individual expression, creativity, innovation, and achievement and in turn helps us better understand and serve our customers. We see ourselves as a place for intellectual curiosity, ideas and debates, where diverse perspectives lead to deeper understanding and better quality results. title: Company Secretary
description: About us:Goodera is the world’s leading employee volunteering platform, powering companies to scale employee volunteering experiences globally through our innovative technology platform and unique operating model. With a presence in over 100 countries and support for 30+ languages, we connect over 500 clients - including 60+ Fortune 500 companies with meaningful volunteer opportunities tailored to their communities. To date, our impact has reached over 10 million beneficiaries, powered by 1 million+ employee volunteers and a network of 50,000+ nonprofit partners. Growing at 100% year on year, we are backed by top investors including Zoom Ventures, Elevation Capital, Nexus Venture Partners, Omidyar Network, and Ursula Burns.About the RoleWe are seeking a qualified Company Secretary to own the corporate secretarial and governance function for the Goodera group, the Indian parent and its overseas entities, as we prepare for a public listing in India. This is a build-and-scale role: you will clean up legacy compliance, institutionalize processes that survive due diligence, and grow with the company into a listed-company secretarial function.You will work directly with Finance, Tax & Compliance, and Legal leadership, and coordinate with statutory auditors, practicing company secretaries, RTAs, merchant bankers, and US counsel.Career arc: For the right candidate, this role is a pathway to Compliance Officer of a listed company under SEBI (LODR) Regulations - one of the most accelerated governance mandates available at this experience level.Responsibilities:Core Secretarial & Statutory Compliance (India)Own the full Companies Act, 2013 compliance calendar: board meetings, committee meetings, general meetings, resolutions, and filings (AOC-4, MGT-7, DIR-3 KYC, event-based forms) across the Indian entity and any Indian subsidiaries.Draft agendas, notices, and minutes in conformity with Secretarial Standards (SS-1 and SS-2); maintain statutory registers and minute books to due-diligence standard.Overhaul and digitize legacy statutory records, registers, and filings so the company is perpetually ready for investor, banker, and regulator diligence.Manage remediation of historical gaps: condonation of delay, compounding applications, revival or strike-off of dormant entities, and re-execution of defective corporate documents.Replace manual tracking with an automated compliance calendar covering ROC/MCA, FEMA/RBI, and (in time) SEBI/stock exchange deadlines with defined owners and escalation.FEMA / RBI & Cross-Border ComplianceHandle inbound investment reporting (FC-GPR, FC-TRS), annual FLA returns, and downstream/ODI compliance for the US subsidiary structure.Support compounding applications and regularization of past reporting delays with RBI/AD banks.Manage FEMA aspects of secondary share transfers, buybacks, and ESOP exercises by resident and non-resident holders, including valuation certificate coordination and pricing-guideline compliance.Coordinate with authorized dealer banks, valuers, and FEMA counsel; maintain a clean audit trail for every cross-border capital transaction.Cap Table, ESOP & Share TransactionsEnd-to-end ESOP administration: grant letters, vesting schedules, exercises, cancellations, surrender/lapse tracking, and pool reconciliation against board and shareholder approvals.Maintain a single-source-of-truth cap table reconciled across the register of members, depository records, and shareholder agreements.Execute share transfer mechanics: DIS processing, demat coordination, Deeds of Adherence, stamp duty, and CP completion for secondary transactions.Drive full dematerialization of shares and manage the RTA and depository (NSDL/CDSL) relationships - a listing precondition.Coordinate with VC investors and institutional board members on approvals, waivers, consents, and information rights under the Shareholders' Agreement; run the mechanics of rights issues, bonus issues, and any pre-IPO restructuring of instruments (e.g., CCPS conversion).IPO ReadinessExecute the secretarial workstream of IPO preparation under leadership direction, including:Conversion from private to public limited company and consequential charter document changes.Board and committee re-constitution: independent director onboarding, Audit Committee, Nomination & Remuneration Committee, Stakeholders' Relationship Committee, Risk Management Committee - with compliant charters.Corporate-approval backbone for the DRHP: authorizations, certifications, and secretarial due-diligence responses to merchant bankers and legal counsel.Policy suite build-out: related party transactions, materiality of events, code of conduct, whistleblower/vigil mechanism, insider trading code and structured digital database (SDD) under SEBI (PIT) Regulations.Secretarial audit under Section 204 and annual secretarial compliance report readiness.Data room ownership for all secretarial, capital, and governance records.Post-Listing Compliance (Knowledge Expectation)This role is designed to mature into the listed-entity compliance function. Candidates must have working knowledge of and will be trained and supported to operate:SEBI (LODR) Regulations: quarterly and event-based disclosures, Regulation 30 materiality framework, corporate governance reports, shareholding patterns, and stock exchange intimations.SEBI (PIT) Regulations: trading window management, pre-clearance, UPSI handling, and SDD maintenance.Listed-company meeting mechanics: e-voting, record dates, dividend compliance, postal ballots, and investor grievance handling (SCORES).Ongoing engagement with stock exchanges, RTA, depositories, and the secretarial auditor.Overseas Entities - Coordination & OversightCoordinate (with US counsel and registered agents - not replace them) the corporate maintenance of the US subsidiary and affiliated US nonprofit: annual state filings, registered agent renewals, board consents and minutes, and officer/director records.Maintain a group-wide entity management tracker: good standing, filing status, intercompany agreements, and authorized signatory records across all entities.Support governance of the group's nonprofit foundation in coordination with its US counsel and auditors: board documentation, conflict-of-interest compliance, and policy maintenance.Ensure Indian-side compliance triggered by overseas entities (ODI reporting, APR filings, board approvals for guarantees/funding).What We Look ForQualification: Member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI).Experience: 4-6 years of post-qualification core secretarial experience. Exposure to any of the following is strongly preferred: IPO/DRHP process, listed-company compliance, PE/VC-funded company secretarial work, or FEMA-heavy transaction work.Technical depth: Companies Act, 2013; Secretarial Standards (SS-1, SS-2); FEMA/RBI reporting (FC-GPR, FC-TRS, FLA, ODI); working knowledge of SEBI (LODR), (ICDR), and (PIT) Regulations.Execution quality: Demonstrated ability to build trackers, registers, and processes from scratch and keep them diligence-ready - not just file on time.Strong plusLL.B. or equivalent legal training.Hands-on IPO or pre-IPO readiness experience (even as part of a team).Experience with demat/RTA processes, ESOP administration at scale, or cross-border group structures.Comfort with compliance tooling and automation (entity management software, compliance calendars, cap table platforms).

title: Manager - GDS Ethics Office
description:
At EY, you’ll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture and technology to become the best version of you. And we’re counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all.
  
  
**Assistant Director – GDS Ethics Office**
This role is part of the GDS Ethics Function, and the individual will support the GDS Ethics team across all countries on areas related to ethics matters and sexual harassment investigations.
  
  
**The opportunity**
This is an exciting time to join the Global Delivery Services (GDS) ethics team as we scale up our program to match the expansion of the business. You will build your professional knowledge and credentials, learn how EY operates globally and work within a cross functional team of professionals to embed and improve the workplace culture by solving Ethics matters across its operating locations in India, Poland, China, the Philippines & Argentina.
  
  
As part of the role, you shall support the Ethics team and be part of the inquiries / investigations and ensure the compliance to the global code of conduct and other organizational processes and procedures.
  
  
**Your Key Responsibilities Require You To**

* Lead ethics team members and support the ethics officer in handling employee grievances and investigations related to workplace / sexual harassment, integrity issues etc. across various Geographies.
* Project / program management including the automation projects
* Lead the review, development and implementation of compliance processes, rules and standards as per the internal policies, automation projects etc.
* Review the investigation and reporting processes for any AI related opportunity implementation.
* Develop a thorough understanding of the governing policies of the Corporate and rules and regulations applicable to relevant geography.
* Support local business functions with Ethics related policy compliances.

* Prepare case reports and ethics dashboards
